news.Title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Intel: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
Semiconductor giants are evolving rapidly as AI demand reshapes the computing landscape. Choosing between Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) requires weighing high-growth momentum against a complex turnaround.

Advanced Micro Devices focuses on high-performance design for data centers and gaming, often outsourcing its manufacturing to stay lean. Intel remains a vertically integrated powerhouse, attempting to balance its chip design business with a massive expansion into third-party foundry services. They compete for dominance in the heart of every modern server and personal computer.

The case for Advanced Micro Devices

Advanced Micro Devices designs high-performance processors and accelerators for the semiconductor stocks category. Its strategy hinges on the Instinct MI450 series GPUs and partnerships with companies like OpenAI. Since it relies on a small number of customers including major cloud providers, customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

According to its latest annual report, filed in early 2026, revenue for FY 2025 reached nearly $34.6 billion, representing growth of approximately 34.3% compared to the prior year. Net income for the period was close to $4.3 billion, and the company reported a net margin of approximately 12.5%. This trend highlights the company's ability to capture share in the lucrative data center market.

Advanced Micro Devices maintains a strong financial position with a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.1x, which measures total debt relative to shareholder equity. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is nearly 2.9x and free cash flow reached roughly $6.7 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 21.2% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Intel

Intel provides processors and software for cloud, edge, and networking uses while scaling its internal and external foundry business. Its customer base primarily consists of original equipment manufacturers and cloud service providers. The company is betting heavily on its ability to manufacture chips for others to rival industry leaders.

According to its latest annual report, filed in early 2026, revenue for FY 2025 reached nearly $52.9 billion, which was a slight decline of approximately 0.5% year over year. The company reported a net loss of close to $267.0 million and a net margin of roughly -0.5% for the year. While this was a vast improvement over the prior year's steep losses, it shows that the turnaround is still in progress.

Story Continues

Intel's balance sheet as of December 2025 shows a debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.4x and a current ratio of approximately 2.0x. Free cash flow was negative, reaching roughly $4.9 billion in outflows as the company continues heavy investment in new factories. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 25.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Risk profile comparison

Advanced Micro Devices faces intense competition from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Intel, particularly in the data center and GPU markets. The company is vulnerable to export controls on shipments to China and must successfully integrate large acquisitions like ZT Systems. Additionally, the cyclical nature of the industry and global economic sensitivity impact demand.

Intel navigates severe competitive pressure from Advanced Micro Devices in the microprocessor and accelerator markets. The company is currently dealing with operational challenges and ongoing litigation related to its corporate governance. Additionally, Intel faces regulatory risks as it attempts to maintain market share while pivoting its business model toward foundry services.

Valuation comparison

Intel offers a significantly lower price-to-sales multiple, while Advanced Micro Devices carries a premium valuation that reflects its faster growth and profitability.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

I'd go with AMD. The company is cementing its position as the primary alternative to Nvidia in the AI chip market, and each quarter keeps coming in stronger than Wall Street anticipated. Its data center business has more than doubled year over year, and the company has posted six consecutive quarters of growth above 30%. And perhaps most exciting, a partnership with Anthropic signals that demand for its chips extends well beyond the current quarter.

Intel's turnaround is gaining momentum in ways that are worth acknowledging. Revenue just grew at its fastest pace in 15 years and the data center business is recovering after years of losing ground. The company has beaten its own guidance seven consecutive quarters. The stock has surged dramatically this year as investors took notice of the results.

Both stocks carry uncertainty right now, but AMD is growing faster, with a cleaner business trajectory and less execution risk. For a patient investor, that combination is the more comfortable starting point.

news.Title: Jim Cramer Believes META Muse Will “Have Much More Market Share Than OpenAI”
news.Content:
During the September 28 episode of Mad Money, Jim Cramer mentioned Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ: META ) and highlighted that its products fit current market demands without risk of demand destruction. He stated:

Members of the CNBC Investing Club know I've been resolute, though, that there are opportunities like the two stocks that I've been recommending now for the last month: Intel and Meta. I know it's boring when I repeat the same stocks relentlessly, but without the repetition, it just doesn't get through. And these have been winners. Why Intel? Why Meta? They fit the moment; that's why. First, their products are in such high demand- one new, one old- that there are no concerns about demand destruction, which is usually the end result when higher interest rates clash with higher prices. Second, they're each in a new product cycle.

Meta has Muse, its personal agentic AI platform that could potentially have several billion users. Personal assistants, whether for consumers or for the enterprise, are irresistible when they're cheap. Muse is free as long as you don't use it too much. I think Meta crushed it with this, and I bet it'll have much more market share than OpenAI, which remains niche compared to the house that Zuckerberg built... Muse, like so many other agentic devices, is a workhorse that runs on CPUs.

In a September episode, we also discussed why Cramer suggested holding on to META .

Agentic Artificial Intelligence Rollout And Revenue Expansion

Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) continues to show exceptional financial strength, driven by strong advertising demand and technological innovation across its Family of Apps. In its second quarter, the company reported revenue of $60.8 billion, up 28% from the same period last year. Artificial intelligence integration has optimized ad targeting and increased user engagement across Facebook and Instagram, helping protect top-line revenue growth.

The introduction of personal agentic platforms like Muse adds a powerful new vector for consumer engagement and future monetization through commerce and advanced assistant services. Furthermore, unlike competitors heavily reliant on specialized graphics processors for every tier of computation, the architectural design of agentic tools operating efficiently on standard central processing units provides a distinct cost and deployment advantage at global scale.

Meta remains one of the leading AI stocks, but investors looking for lower-priced opportunities may want to see which names made our list of 10 Best AI Stocks to Buy Under $25.

Story Continues

Capital Expenditure Intensity And Regulatory Pressures

Despite solid revenue growth, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) faces notable capital allocation pressures and regulatory headwinds that require careful evaluation. Capital expenditures have surged as management builds out massive artificial intelligence infrastructure, data centers, and advanced compute clusters to support long-term strategic initiatives. For the current year, the company expects capital expenditures in the range of $130-145 billion, almost doubling from last year and up from the prior outlook of $125-145 billion. The heavy spending commitments require continuous top-line advertising growth to protect free cash margins against potential diminishing returns on capital investments.

Additionally, the company navigates complex legal scrutiny and regulatory challenges regarding data privacy practices across global markets, highlighted by recent courtroom verdicts and compliance requirements. Macroeconomic shifts impacting digital advertising budgets or a slower-than-expected monetization timeline for new generative offerings could also introduce near-term volatility for the equity.

Hedge Fund Positions and Short Sentiment

According to Insider Monkey database tracking covering institutional portfolios, 254 hedge funds held positions in the company at the close of the second quarter, reflecting a slight shift from 262 funds in the prior quarter. Meanwhile, short seller activity remains exceptionally muted, with short interest accounting for roughly 1.41% of the float.

Taking together Cramer's insight on demand resilience, the powerful revenue generation from digital advertising, the architectural efficiency of CPU-backed agentic AI platforms like Muse, and the manageable weight of heavy capital expenditures, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) trades at a forward P/E multiple of 22x, a seemingly reasonable valuation that offers a compelling entry point relative to its growth trajectory. Supported by these fundamentals, the stock stands out as a well-supported multi-year winner heading into its upcoming financial reports.

While we acknowledge the potential of META as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. If you're looking for an extremely undervalued AI stock that also stands to benefit significantly from Trump-era tariffs and the onshoring trend, see our free report on the best short-term AI stock .

news.Title: 台股5萬點近在眼前　少年股神勇敢殺進殺出
news.Content:
台股一路衝新高，投資人數跟著暴增，其中年輕世代為新一波開戶主力。證交所公布最新統計，9月累計總開戶人數攀升至1,476.3萬人，單月增加6.5萬人、續創歷史新高。其中30歲以下新增約4.1萬人，占當月新增人數逾6成，等於每新增10名投資人，就有超過6人未滿30歲。

近幾個月台股歷經震盪，8月重新站回4.4萬點後，9月再攻上4.8萬點，10月以來更接連改寫歷史新高。今(5)天在權值股領軍下大漲1,236.3點，收4萬9,712.04點，距離5萬點大關近在咫尺，成交值也放大至1兆1,508億元。

指數頻頻創高，吸引更多民眾加入投資行列。9月開戶數成長最快是未滿20歲的「少年股神」。0至19歲開戶數單月飆升2.1萬人，累計達89萬人，占整體6.03%；20至30歲則上揚1.9萬人，累計193萬人，占比13.07%。兩者合計，30歲以下開戶人數約282.1萬人，占全市場19.1%，相當於每5個證券戶中，就有近1個來自30歲以下族群。

年輕人成為開戶最積極的一群，而中高齡族群則撐住投資人口基本盤。31至40歲累計239.1萬人、41至50歲273.5萬人、51至60歲241.6萬人；61歲以上更有428萬人，占比28.99%，穩居各年齡層之冠。41歲以上合計占整體開戶近64%，呈現新增人口快速年輕化、整體存量仍以中高齡為主的結構。

性別分布也出現明顯的世代差異。9月女性開戶數761.2萬人，高於男性703.1萬人；但30歲以下反而是男性較多，0至19歲男性比女性多約3.7萬人，20至30歲也多約2.4萬人。自31歲以上開始，各年齡層則全面轉為女性開戶數領先。隨著台股投資熱度升高，年輕人陸續投入，使投資人口的年齡與性別版圖同步出現變化。

news.Title: Are stocks expensive? This 30-year-low stat says otherwise.
news.Content: Big names in tech such as Nvidia ( NVDA ) and AMD ( AMD ) may have just ripped to record highs, but that doesn't mean the overall stock market is overheated. In fact, investors could make the argument that stocks look downright cheap. One piece of evidence for that is the price-to-earnings growth ratio, better known as the PEG ratio. It measures a stock's valuation relative to its expected earnings growth, with a lower PEG ratio generally suggesting a more attractive valuation. The S&P 500's PEG ratio just hit a 30-year low, according to data from Yardeni Research (see chart below). With the outlook for corporate earnings remaining robust, it almost makes no sense to see such a low PEG ratio. As of today, the S&P 500 is expected to report year-over-year earnings growth of 29.5% for the recently completed third quarter. If 29.5% is the actual growth rate for the quarter, it will mark the third consecutive quarter of earnings growth above 25%, according to FactSet. It would also represent the eighth straight quarter of double-digit percentage earnings growth. For the fourth quarter, Wall Street analysts are calling for earnings growth of 27.6%. Analysts are predicting year-over-year earnings growth of 32.4% for 2026 when all is said and done. "The bull market continues to deserve the benefit of the doubt. Beneath the surface, a healthy reset in prices and valuations is creating opportunities as the fourth quarter begins," Truist chief strategist Keith Lerner said, adding, "Still, the weight of the evidence currently supports remaining overweight equities, maintaining our preference for U.S. growth, and selectively adding income opportunities." news.Title: Nasdaq notches record high close as investors focus on earnings
news.Content:
By Noel Randewich and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Oct 5 (Reuters) - The Nasdaq notched a record high close on Monday, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, as investors focused on a dip ‌in oil prices and looked ahead to quarterly earnings reports.

It was the Nasdaq's second ‌day of sharp gains after weaker-than-expected jobs data on Friday dampened expectations for an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve ​at its policy meeting this month.

AI heavyweight Nvidia and Microsoft gained ground.

Meta Platforms and Tesla also rose.

Oil prices slipped after crude exports from the Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies.

"With the economic data calendar being light and earnings about a week away, investors are really ‌groping for anything positive to glom ⁠onto, and clearly they're looking at lower energy prices," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.

BANKS KICK OFF THIRD-QUARTER RESULTS

Third-quarter earnings season kicks ⁠off next week with reports from large US banks.

Analysts on average see S&P 500 earnings jumping over 30% year over year, thanks largely to AI-related stocks, according to LSEG data.

Following jobs data on Friday that ​showed US ​job growth slowed more than expected in September, traders ​see a 24% chance of an ‌interest rate hike at the Fed's October meeting, down from a 70% chance a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

PTC surged after France's Schneider Electric agreed to acquire the software firm in a $22.6 billion all-cash deal.

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 gained 51.50 points, or 0.67%, to end at 7,774.22 points, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 289.42 points, or 1.06%, to 27,480.28. The Dow Jones ‌Industrial Average rose 94.59 points, or 0.18%, to 51,274.32.

The ​Nasdaq's previous record high close was on September 22.

Optimism about ​robust corporate earnings has helped US stocks ​outperform global rivals in the last six months, despite rising Treasury yields and ‌higher oil prices related to the US ​war with Iran.

RXO jumped after ​freight forwarding firm C.H. Robinson Worldwide agreed to buy the transportation broker in a stock-and-cash transaction for $5.8 billion. C.H. Robinson fell.

Cerebras Systems rose after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on ​social media the chip designer ‌is a "close partner" and that the companies have "deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed."

(Reporting ​by Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Shashwat Chauhan in Bengaluru and by Noel Randewich in San ​Francisco; Editing by Devika Syamnath and Rod Nickel)

news.Title: TSMC stock hits all-time high after Elon Musk confirms early Terafab talks
news.Content:
What happened: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company ( TSM ) stock rose to an all-time high on Monday.

What's behind the move: The rise in TSMC stock comes after Elon Musk acknowledged early-stage talks with Taiwan Semiconductor about a potential collaboration on his Terafab semiconductor initiative.

In a recent newsletter, tech journalist Tim Culpan said, "TSMC is exploring ways to work with Elon Musk's Terafab to help the startup chipmaker run its new semiconductor factories in Texas, my sources tell me."

Musk responded to a screenshot of the letter saying, "Just discussions, but something may come of it," on X over the weekend .

Terafab is Musk's plan to build a giant semiconductor factory to serve Tesla ( TSLA ), SpaceX ( SPCX ), and xAI.

US chipmaker Intel ( INTC ), which joined Terafab back in April, declined more than 2%.

What else you need to know: TSMC is the world's largest foundry, and its business has boomed, driven by demand for semiconductors used in artificial intelligence.

The company is undergoing significant expansion in the US as part of a multiyear plan to manufacture chips for its clients, including Apple ( AAPL ), Nvidia ( NVDA ), and AMD ( AMD ).

The stock is up more than 60% year to date.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) is pushing its artificial-intelligence strategy deeper into the business market, and Jefferies believes the move could eventually unlock a much larger monetization opportunity across the company's existing base of business customers. Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The latest push includes Meta Enterprise Platform and Muse for Small Business , along with the hiring of former MongoDB CEO CJ Desai as Meta's new Chief Enterprise Platform Officer. Jefferies analyst Brent Thill said Desai brings more than three decades of experience across product, engineering, infrastructure, business applications and security. According to Thill, Desai will oversee efforts to bring Meta's broader AI stack to businesses, including Muse Agent, Meta Business Agent, Muse API and Muse Code . The opportunity is potentially significant because Meta already has more than 200 million businesses on its platforms . META has >200M businesses on its platform, which are heavily undermonetized, Thill wrote. Jefferies believes AI could help Meta attract more businesses and eventually increase monetization across that customer base. Still, the firm does not expect the enterprise push to become an immediate earnings driver. Meta remains better known as a consumer social-media company than an enterprise software vendor, meaning it has to prove that businesses will trust and adopt its AI tools at scale. Thill said CIOs Jefferies has spoken with see promise in Meta's enterprise AI ambitions, particularly around the company's open-source AI models. What Meta Investors Should Watch Muse for Small Business could become an important early test. The assistant can help companies analyze business data, identify potential customers and create marketing content. Muse is a compelling assistant for small businesses, but monetization will take time, Thill said. For investors, the key metrics will be business adoption, engagement, pricing and whether Meta can convert its huge existing merchant base into paying AI customers. The opportunity is substantial, but the execution challenge is equally important. If Meta proves it can extend its AI stack beyond consumers and advertising into recurring business software revenue, its addressable market could expand meaningfully. For now, however, Jefferies sees the enterprise push as a long-term opportunity rather than a near-term revenue catalyst. news.Title: Morgan Stanley revisits Micron stock price target amid stellar growth
news.Content: For decades, memory chips followed a painful script. Companies expanded capacity amid rising demand, translating into higher margins. A few years later, slowing demand meant an oversupply of products, which drove profits down. Artificial intelligence may be tearing up that script. And one of Wall Street's most closely followed chip analysts just weighed in on whether Micron's remarkable run has room left. Why Micron stock rides the AI memory boom Every AI model needs a ton of memory driven by bigger models, longer conversations, and a widening user base. Micron (MU) Chairman and CEO Sanjay Mehrotra put it plainly on the company's Sept. 30 earnings call. AI platforms deliver more value with more memory and faster memory. That demand has turned Micron into a cash machine. Fiscal 2026 revenue reached a record $133.2 billion, up 256% from the prior year, CFO Mark Murphy said on the call. Also Read: A chipmaker's boom is quietly raising the price of your electronics Gross margin expanded to 81.1%, a 40-point jump, while earnings per share soared 811% to $75.52. The fiscal fourth quarter , which ended in August, was even stronger: Revenue: A record $54.2 billion, up 379% from a year earlier and the sixth straight quarterly record DRAM revenue: A record $39.8 billion, or 73% of total sales Data center SSD revenue: Nearly $10 billion, more than 10 times the level a year earlier Gross margin: 87%, up 2.1 percentage points from the prior quarter Free cash flow: $33.2 billion Micron expects fiscal first quarter revenue of $61.5 billion and earnings of $38.15 per share. The forecast came in well above what Wall Street analysts expected, which was $57.4 billion in revenue and $35.47 per share, according to a Morgan Stanley research report shared with me. Morgan Stanley holds its Micron stock price target Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore kept an "Overweight" rating and a $1,200 price target on Micron in an Oct. 1 research note titled "Micron makes the case that it's better for longer." At the time of writing, MU stock trades at $1,074, so the target implies about 10% upside. The firm did reset its numbers, though. Morgan Stanley lifted its fiscal 2027 earnings estimate to $182.52 per share from $168.52. Its revenue forecast climbed to $281 billion from $266.9 billion. More Micron: Michael Burry increases his bet against popular chip giant Bank of America doubles down on Micron stock after AI bombshell Micron stock jumps as investors look beyond GPUs in AI chip trade Does Micron pay dividends? Its yield and payouts explained Story Continues "We said in our preview and in recent notes that the debate has shifted from 'how good can it get' to 'how long it can stay good,'" Moore wrote. Here's the twist. Micron's beats are getting smaller. Over the prior three quarters, it topped consensus earnings estimates by 20% to 40%. This time, the beat was 5% and guided 6% above consensus. Moore doesn't see that as a red flag. He thinks it may be "the new normal as Micron's visibility improves." Also read: Who owns Micron Technology? A look at its top investors Why Micron's supply crunch matters Building memory capacity takes years, clean rooms take a long time to construct, and production ramps slowly, even after the first wafers roll out. Mehrotra offered the most striking comment of the call. "Even with additional industry DRAM clean room space plans with robust demand trends, including new upside requests from customers, we do not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance." Customers are acting on that fear. Micron has signed 26 strategic customer agreements, known as SCAs. These are multiyear take-or-pay deals that lock in supply. Related: Micron's memory boom faces a new test Customers have committed $32 billion, mostly cash deposits. Mehrotra said more than 75% of Micron's 2027 output is already spoken for. Moore called the longer contracts "a testament to the customer anxieties about securing DRAM even 5 years from now." He added that, on Morgan Stanley's new estimates, Micron will earn close to half its current $1.23 trillion market value by the end of 2028. Murphy said Micron plans to return 100% of its excess cash to shareholders over time, with a step up starting Dec. 9. What could cool the Micron stock price The rally hasn't been linear. Moore said investors trimmed bullish forecasts in July for a few reasons. A trillion-dollar memory market can't keep raising prices at this pace forever. Long-term contracts include price ceilings. And AI customers are learning to do more with less memory. The once popular $300 earnings call now looks less likely, Moore said. Morgan Stanley sees about $200 for calendar 2027 and calls that conservative. The firm's bull case puts the stock at $1,650. Its bear case, where memory slides into a downturn in 2027, sits at $675. Two catalysts remain. Repricing of high bandwidth memory, or HBM, could add roughly $9 to quarterly earnings per share, Moore estimated. A larger buyback authorization is also coming. For a business famous for boom and bust, "better for longer" might be the most bullish phrase of all. news.Title: Nasdaq hits record high as investors focus on earnings
news.Content:
By Noel Randewich and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Oct 5 (Reuters) - The Nasdaq hit an all-time high on Monday, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, as investors focused on a dip in oil prices and looked ‌ahead to quarterly earnings reports.

It was the Nasdaq's second straight intraday record high after weaker-than-expected jobs ‌data on Friday dampened expectations for an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting this month.

The S&P 500 climbed and ​was about 0.5% below its intraday record high on August 13.

AI heavyweight Nvidia rose 1.6%, while Microsoft added 1.5%.

Meta Platforms added 2.1% and Tesla climbed 2.5%.

Oil prices slipped after crude exports from the Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies.

"With the economic data calendar being light and earnings about a week away, investors ‌are really groping for anything positive to ⁠glom onto, and clearly they're looking at lower energy prices," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.

BANKS KICK OFF THIRD-QUARTER RESULTS

Third-quarter earnings season kicks off next week ⁠with reports from large US banks.

Analysts on average see S&P 500 earnings jumping over 30% year over year, thanks largely to AI-related stocks, according to LSEG data.

Following jobs data on Friday that showed US job growth slowed more than expected in ​September, ​traders see a 24% chance of an interest rate hike ​at the Fed's October meeting, down from a ‌70% chance a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

PTC surged 34% after France's Schneider Electric agreed to acquire the software firm in a $22.6 billion all-cash deal.

The S&P 500 was up 0.68% at 7,775.33 points, lifting its 2026 gain to almost 14%.

The Nasdaq rose 0.98% to 27,458.40 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 0.25% at 51,306.65 points.

Ten of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by materials, up 1.46%, followed by a ‌1.22% gain in energy.

Optimism about robust corporate earnings has helped US ​stocks outperform global rivals in the last six months, despite rising ​Treasury yields and higher oil prices related to ​the US war with Iran.

RXO jumped 29% after freight forwarding firm C.H. Robinson Worldwide agreed ‌to buy the transportation broker in a stock-and-cash ​transaction for $5.8 billion. C.H. Robinson ​fell 12%.

Cerebras Systems rose 8% after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the chip designer is a "close partner" and that the companies have "deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed."

Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the ​S&P 500 by a 2.4-to-1 ratio.

The ‌S&P 500 posted 12 new highs and 19 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 47 new highs and ​216 new lows.

(Reporting by Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Shashwat Chauhan in Bengaluru and by Noel Randewich ​in San Francisco; Editing by Devika Syamnath and Rod Nickel)

【記者柯安聰台北報導】台股5萬點近在咫尺，台股基金績效更大放異彩！今年前3季，145檔台股基金中，高達125檔報酬跑贏大盤；國內可銷售的境內外共同基金共有43檔報酬翻倍，其中39檔更由台股基金包辦，占比逾9成。亮眼成績背後，投資人也擔心高利率、油價與AI獲利前景，猶豫現在進場是否買在高點。「鉅亨買基金」表示，創高後能否續漲，關鍵在企業獲利與成長動能。看好台股者可分批參與，並保留回檔加碼的餘裕，避免因追逐績效而一次重押。

根據理柏環球截至9月底統計，台股前3季上漲68.1%，16檔台灣中小型股票基金全數超越大盤，129檔台灣股票基金也有109檔勝出。進一步觀察報酬翻倍的基金，台灣股票基金占33檔，最高報酬達146%；台灣中小型股票基金占6檔，最高更達160.5%，居所有基金之冠。「鉅亨買基金」總經理張榮仁指出，台股基金不只拿下多數翻倍席次，更有廣泛超越大盤的表現，展現經理人掌握產業輪動與選股的優勢。

亮眼績效能否延續至第4季，仍要回到AI需求與企業獲利檢視。張榮仁表示，台灣在晶片製造、伺服器與相關設備供應鏈具備優勢，全球AI建設持續推進，有助企業承接需求。市場雖關注龐大投資何時回收，但AI付費使用與商業應用也正擴大，後續應觀察需求能否持續轉化為訂單、營收與現金流。投資回收需要時間，成長機會卻可能提前反映在股價上；由於各家企業受惠程度不同，能否辨識具實質獲利潛力的企業，將更考驗基金經理人的選股能力。

除了成長能否兌現，高殖利率與油價也是影響後市的重要變數。張榮仁指出，長債殖利率走高，除了通膨因素，也反映政府發債與企業融資需求增加。資金成本上升會對股市評價形成壓力，但若營收與獲利持續成長，企業仍有能力承受。油價上漲則可能推升運輸與生產成本，是否進一步引發廣泛通膨，仍須觀察漲勢的持續性及傳導程度。因此，高利率與高油價固然需要留意，但能否改變股市走勢，還要看其對經濟成長與企業獲利的實際影響。

即使看好基本面，「現在買會不會站在山頂」仍是許多投資人的心結。張榮仁表示，指數創高代表突破過去價格，並不等於後續沒有上漲空間。鉅亨買基金回測標普500指數自1957年以來資料，在創歷史新高後的下一交易日進場，持有5年的平均累積價格報酬達50.9%。這項美股經驗雖不能直接推論台股表現，仍提醒投資人，單憑「已經漲很多」而持續等待，可能錯過後續成長。對買點有所顧慮者，可透過分次投入分散進場時點，減少反覆猜測高低點的壓力。

張榮仁強調，前3季績效讓台股基金成為市場焦點，第4季布局則應從過去的報酬，進一步看向未來的成長。挑選基金時，應兼顧長期表現、選股策略與回檔風險，透過定期定額持續累積，也可搭配「鉅亨超底王」，在達到設定跌幅時自動加碼，並預留足夠資金。已有持倉者則應檢視台股與科技部位是否過度集中，適度調整配置。面對5萬點關卡，掌握獲利前景、安排投入節奏，比單憑指數高低決定進出，更有助於兼顧投資機會與承受波動的能力。（自立電子報2026/10/5）

news.Title: Could Sandisk Stock Double in Value in 12 Months?
news.Content:
The past year has been a tremendous one for Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK), as it has rallied an incredible 1,200%. But at $250 billion in market cap, it's still not among the top tech companies in the world in terms of valuation.

Sandisk's stock has been taking a breather in recent months as it's down around 27% from the high of $2,354 that it hit earlier this year. With a reduced valuation and plenty of growth opportunities due to the ongoing memory shortage, could the tech stock double in value within the next 12 months?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Analysts still see plenty of upside for the stock

While there may be less excitement around Sandisk's stock these days, analysts remain optimistic that it can go higher in the near term. Of 28 analyst ratings, 24 rate the stock a buy (the others are just 'hold'). The consensus analyst price target for Micron is just under $2,114, which implies an upside of around 24% from where it's trading right now.

Analyst price targets reflect expectations about where analysts think the stock will go in the short term, typically over the next 12 to 18 months. While a 24% gain is encouraging, the consensus suggests the stock isn't likely to double within the next 12 months.

However, if the company's upcoming earnings report features a rosy outlook and a significant upgrade to its guidance, analysts could very well raise their price targets for the stock.

The stock may seem cheap, but I don't think it'll double

Sandisk has achieved impressive growth in recent quarters, and so the stock is trading modestly related to earnings -- its price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple is 23, which is in line with what the S&P 500 average is. But with Sandisk, its growth potential is massive, and thus, it may warrant a higher multiple . Based on its projected future profits, its forward P/E multiple is just eight.

However, investors don't appear willing to pay more for the stock due to uncertainty about how long the memory shortage will last. Once it ends, demand could slow significantly, and prices may also come down. Sandisk and other memory stocks could be vulnerable to significant declines.

Given the uncertainty, investors may thus not be as willing to price Sandisk's stock much higher than where it is right now. While it may still rise in value, particularly if its earnings results and guidance remain promising, I don't think it'll double in value within the next 12 months.

news.Title: 3 Stocks From AI & Energy to Buy Before Q3 Earnings Kick Off
news.Content:
The third-quarter earnings season is approaching with a strong backdrop. Going by the latest Earnings Preview, the S&P 500 earnings are set to increase 24.6% year over year in the to-be-reported quarter on 11.6% higher revenues, marking the eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit earnings growth. More importantly, for investors seeking stocks with the potential to outperform expectations, the positive revisions trend has remained intact, with estimates for both the current and subsequent quarters moving higher.

Technology and Energy stand out in this environment. Per the earnings preview, third-quarter earnings are expected to rise 43.3% for Technology and 114.3% for Energy, putting both well ahead of the broader market. The semiconductor industry is particularly strong, with earnings projected to jump 85.5% on 62.8% higher revenues. Energy has received the most pronounced upward revision to its third-quarter earnings outlook since the quarter began, reflecting the impact of elevated oil prices following disruptions in the Persian Gulf.

Against this backdrop, Lam Research LRCX, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing TSM or TSMC and Marathon Petroleum MPC offer exposure to the two strongest industries with catalysts for potentially exceeding expectations.

Why AI and Energy Could Lead Q3 Earnings

The earnings story of the technology space is no longer dependent entirely on a handful of mega-cap companies. Per Zacks estimates, the technology space's third-quarter earnings growth would still be 20.5%, excluding NVIDIA NVDA, Micron and Alphabet, compared with 43.3% including them. Semiconductor earnings are expected to increase 85.5%, after growth of 110.1% and 96% in the preceding two quarters. That progression indicates that the AI investment cycle is continuing to translate into actual semiconductor demand rather than remaining solely a capital-spending narrative.

The underlying demand environment also remains unusually strong. Reuters reported in late September that the ongoing AI infrastructure investment boom is expected to remain a major driver of economic and corporate growth. Deutsche Bank strategist George Saravelos described the AI investment cycle as a key force supporting markets, while Reuters noted that roughly one-third of current U.S. GDP growth was estimated to be coming from the AI spending surge. The same analysis characterized the current AI capex boom as one of the largest since World War II.

The energy sector has received the strongest positive revisions to its third-quarter earnings outlook since the beginning of the quarter because of elevated oil prices related to the Persian Gulf situation. Energy earnings are now expected to rise more than 114%, substantially exceeding the growth expected for technology and the S&P 500.

Story Continues

Oil prices have remained elevated even as some Gulf exports have recovered. Reuters reported on Oct. 5 that Brent crude remained above $100 per barrel, with logistical constraints, higher tanker costs and limited refining capacity continuing to disrupt the global oil market. Reuters noted that tanker freight rates on some Middle East to Asia routes had surged dramatically, illustrating why physical-market disruptions remain important even as crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz recover.

3 Stocks to Buy Before Earnings

Lam Research: It is expected to have benefited from rising semiconductor capital intensity, particularly in memory and advanced packaging. The company generated $6.72 billion in fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter revenues, up 30% year over year, while adjusted EPS rose 35% to $1.82. Management guided for September-quarter revenues of $8.1 billion, plus or minus $400 million, and adjusted EPS of $2.15, plus or minus 15 cents.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal first-quarter 2027 (ending September 2026) is pegged at $8.12 billion for revenues and $2.17 for EPS, suggesting year-over-year growth of 52.4% and 72.2%, respectively. LRCX is scheduled to report fiscal first-quarter results on Oct. 21 and carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

news.Title: Here's What a $1,000 Investment in Alphabet Stock Could Be Worth in 5 Years. (Hint: It Could More Than Double.)
news.Content:
In my view, one of the most intriguing megacap artificial intelligence stocks to buy and hold over the next five years is Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG). The company has the most complete AI stack and multiple built-in advantages. With $1,000, an investor can buy three shares of the AI stock .

Throughout history, one of the biggest advantages a company can have is distribution, whether that be Coca-Cola with soda or Microsoft with its pre-installed operating system and software bundles on PCs. This is no different with AI, and that is one area where Alphabet continues to shine.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Alphabet has essentially established itself as the gateway to the internet. This comes through its ownership of the world's most used browser and smartphone operating system, Chrome and Android, as well as a revenue-sharing deal to be the default search engine on Apple devices, which helps it capture much of the rest of the market. Thanks to this, Alphabet can get its Gemini-model-powered AI solutions front and center with consumers without them having to download separate apps or change their normal routines. Tools like AI Overviews and AI Mode bring AI directly to consumers, while its powerful two-sided ad network helps it monetize consumer AI better than new frontier model start-ups.

The company's biggest edge, though, is on the hardware side. Alphabet was at the forefront of developing custom chips to run its operation more than a decade ago, and built its entire hardware and software stack around its tensor processing units (TPUs). As a result, it now has the most powerful custom AI accelerators. This benefits it in a few ways.

First, it helps train its Gemini model and run inference at a much lower cost than companies that rely on Nvidia 's graphics processing units (GPUs). Together with its distribution and ad network advantages, this puts it in a strong position in consumer AI. Second, Alphabet realizes better returns on its cloud computing investments when it uses its own chips. The company has said it expects to see a return on its AI infrastructure investments within two years, but that this is halved when it can use its own chips.

Finally, Alphabet's TPUs have proven so powerful that Anthropic has begun buying them directly for use in its own data centers. The two companies, together with co-developer partner Broadcom , signed an agreement in which Broadcom will deliver the chips to Anthropic. This creates another high-margin revenue stream for Alphabet. Altogether, Anthropic has committed to spending about $200 billion with Google Cloud over the next five years.

Story Continues

Where could Alphabet trade in five years?

Analysts are currently expecting solid growth from Alphabet over the next several years. The current consensus projects revenue to climb from just under $500 billion this year to $1.13 trillion in 2031. Adjusted earnings per share, meanwhile, are projected to jump from $11.81 in 2026 to $29.07 in 2021.

If we assume Alphabet's adjusted EPS grows by about 15% in 2032, that would bring it to about $33.43. The stock currently trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) of nearly 29 times, but let's assume, as growth slows, that the multiple compresses a little. Placing a 20 to 25 times forward P/E multiple on the stock would have it trading between $670 and $835 in five years. A $1,000 investment would be worth between $2,000 and $2,500 in 2031. That's between a 100% return at the low end and nearly 150% at the high end.

I'd view that more as a base case, since I think the company could see greater growth in its AI infrastructure and chip business. It also has bets on robotaxis (Waymo) and quantum computing that could potentially start to pay off in five years. As such, Alphabet stock looks like a buy now.

news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Melius analyst Ben Reitzes upgraded Microsoft to Buy from Hold and raised his price target to $665 , implying roughly 28% upside from the share price cited in the report. The shift marks a notable reversal from earlier concerns around Azure and Copilot. Reitzes now believes enterprises are becoming more cautious about how they deploy AI models and agents, creating demand for trusted platforms that can control model access, manage agent behavior and add security and governance layers. The stronger security and governance opportunity could also support Microsoft's pricing power across products including its E7 suite and Fabric . Microsoft is scheduled to report fiscal first-quarter 2027 earnings on October 27 , followed by its Ignite conference in November. Investors should watch whether Azure growth continues accelerating, whether Microsoft can monetize security and governance around AI agents, and whether management provides evidence that enterprise customers increasingly prefer Microsoft as the control layer for AI deployment. If that thesis plays out, the current AI risk narrative could become a source of incremental growth rather than disruption. news.Title: Google Faces New Antitrust Threat in Key Market
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Alphabet's Google ( NASDAQ:GOOG ) is facing another regulatory challenge in Europe after Poland's antitrust watchdog said it suspects the company of abusing its dominant position in negotiations with local media publishers.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with SPCX.

Is GOOG fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The investigation centers on how Google negotiates payments for displaying articles and snippets across Google Search, Google News and Discover .

Poland's Office of Competition and Consumer Protection, known as UOKiK , alleges Google failed to provide publishers with enough information to properly evaluate the company's payment offers.

That information gap, according to the regulator, could have weakened publishers' bargaining position and made negotiations less balanced.

Big tech companies cannot place themselves above the law, UOKiK President Tomasz Chrostny said.

He added that the lack of data made negotiations illusory and could have resulted in Google effectively imposing terms on publishers.

The stakes are potentially significant.

Polish competition rules allow regulators to impose fines of up to 10% of a company's turnover for abuse of a dominant market position.

For Alphabet, the case adds to a broader pattern of regulatory scrutiny surrounding how large technology platforms compensate publishers and structure digital-market relationships.

Investors Takeaway

The biggest question is whether the Polish case remains relatively contained or becomes another precedent for how European regulators approach publisher compensation.

Investors should watch whether UOKiK formally escalates the case, what data disclosure requirements Google may face, and whether any financial penalties or negotiated changes follow.

The headline risk is the potential fine, but the more important long-term issue is whether Google is forced to change the economics or transparency of its publisher agreements.

Any broader shift in how Google pays for news content could affect costs across Search, News and Discover, particularly if similar standards spread to other European markets.

news.Title: Qualcomm's New Huawei Deal Has Bigger Stakes
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Qualcomm ( NASDAQ:QCOM ) and Huawei have reached a new multi-year patent licensing agreement covering 5G, computing, artificial intelligence and networking technologies, deepening a relationship that has previously been defined by both cooperation and major patent disputes. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with QCOM. Is QCOM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The agreement includes cross-licenses to the companies' respective patent portfolios , giving each side broader access to technologies covered by the other's intellectual property. Qualcomm will also purchase certain Huawei U.S. patents tied to computing, AI, networking and other technologies. The transaction remains subject to regulatory approvals. For Qualcomm, the agreement reinforces the importance of licensing alongside its chip business. The company has long generated substantial revenue from intellectual property tied to wireless standards, making broad patent agreements strategically important even when they do not directly involve semiconductor sales. Huawei, meanwhile, has increasingly positioned intellectual property as a revenue-generating asset. The Chinese technology company said its IP licensing business has generated positive revenue since 2021 and that it held more than 165,000 active granted patents at the end of 2025 . The latest deal also follows a major settlement between the two companies in 2020. At that time, Huawei agreed to pay Qualcomm $1.8 billion in back licensing fees to resolve a patent dispute. Investors Takeaway The key issue is whether the new agreement improves the durability and visibility of Qualcomm's licensing business. Investors should watch for any disclosure around the financial terms, the scope of the acquired Huawei patents and whether regulatory review affects the timing of the transaction. The deal also highlights the growing value of patents outside traditional mobile connectivity, particularly in AI, computing and networking. For Qualcomm, expanding access to those technologies could strengthen its intellectual-property position as the company pushes further beyond smartphones into broader computing and AI markets. news.Title: Why Isn't Micron's Stock Taking Off After Reporting Strong Q4 Numbers?
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) released its latest earnings numbers last week, which yet again showed impressive growth on both its top and bottom lines.

But despite the seemingly strong results, the stock hasn't been taking off in value. Is this a sign that these types of results are already baked into the share price, and that Micron's stock may be approaching a peak, or could there be other concerns weighing on investors' minds?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Micron posted a beat-and-raise quarter

For Micron's most recent quarter, which ended on Sept. 3, the company's revenue came in at $54.2 billion, which was nearly five times the $11.32 billion it reported in the same period a year ago. Significant growth, however, is to be expected these days from the business. What matters is whether it beats expectations, which it did; analysts were expecting a little under $51.1 billion. Micron also beat expectations on the bottom line, and its guidance for the current quarter was also better than Wall Street expectations.

The big unknown weighing on the tech stock , however, is how long the current memory shortage will last. While there have been reports that it may not end for at least a couple of years, there is also no shortage of skeptics. Acer CEO Jason Chen has gone so far as to question if there is even a shortage to begin with, given that Chinese companies are ramping up production capacity. Chen believes that companies are simply trying to protect margins. And it's these concerns that may very well be weighing on Micron's stock these days, preventing it from going a whole lot higher.

Why Micron's stock may not be as cheap as it looks

Many investors may point to Micron's low earnings multiple as proof that the stock still has plenty of upside, as it's trading at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of only seven. That's based on analyst expectations of how profitable it will be in the year ahead.

The problem, however, is that it's based on assumptions and forecasts, which can change due to market conditions. And two or three years from now, the forecast may not be as promising. Once the shortage ends, prices may fall sharply.

There's a fair bit of hesitance around Micron's stock, despite the terrific numbers it posted recently. The reality is that this is a riskier and more expensive stock than it may appear to be at first glance. Forward-looking investors will look for early signs to sell the stock before the good times end, which is why the stock's gains depend more on the outlook for the memory market than on the company's earnings numbers.

news.Title: Palantir Stock Surges 42% in 3 Months: Is PLTR Worth Buying?
news.Content:
Palantir Technologies PLTR has gained roughly 42% over the past three months, reflecting growing investor confidence in the company's artificial intelligence strategy, accelerating commercial adoption and expanding government presence. While the share-price rally raises valuation concerns, PLTR's improving economics and increasingly entrenched position within customer operations strengthen the long-term investment case.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Palantir's Ontology Creates a Powerful Enterprise Foundation

One of Palantir's most important competitive advantages is its Ontology framework. Rather than treating enterprise information as disconnected data points, the platform models an organization around the real-world assets, customers, orders, facilities and operational relationships that define its business.

This structure allows applications to act on enterprise information within established rules, permissions and workflows. As a result, Palantir is positioned to become more than an analytics vendor. Its software can operate as a digital foundation connecting data, decisions and business processes.

The investment case becomes particularly compelling as artificial intelligence adoption expands. More capable AI models alone do not guarantee meaningful business outcomes. Enterprises still need systems that connect models with trusted data, workflows and controlled actions. Palantir's Artificial Intelligence Platform, or AIP, addresses this gap by helping organizations deploy AI within operational environments rather than keeping it confined to experimental applications.

Once a customer builds its initial use case around Palantir's platform, additional applications can be created on the same underlying structure. This potentially improves returns on the original implementation while increasing the difficulty and cost of replacing the platform.

Growth and Customer Spending Remain Exceptional

Palantir delivered another exceptionally strong quarter, with revenues reaching $1.94 billion and advancing 93% year over year. U.S. commercial revenues rose 149% to $764 million, while U.S. government revenues climbed 90% to $809 million.

The company also generated a GAAP operating margin of 47%, while adjusted free cash flow reached $1.22 billion, representing a margin of 63%. Net dollar retention increased to 157% from 150% sequentially, indicating that existing customers are significantly expanding their use of Palantir products.

U.S. commercial customer count rose 35% year over year to 653. The contrast between customer growth and revenue expansion is particularly noteworthy. Palantir is generating substantially more revenue from existing customers as organizations broaden deployments after initial adoption.

Story Continues

This dynamic supports the argument that Palantir's platforms become more valuable as customers build additional applications on top of their established digital infrastructure.

Improving Deployment Efficiency Could Unlock More Growth

Another potential catalyst lies in Palantir's deployment model. Historically, the company has relied heavily on highly skilled engineers to work closely with customers during implementation. That approach can accelerate value creation but may also limit how quickly Palantir can onboard new customers.

Greater automation and self-service capabilities could therefore represent an important next phase of growth. If PLTR can reduce the level of manual engineering required for new deployments while maintaining implementation quality, it could accelerate customer additions without needing a comparable expansion in sales or technical headcount.

Such operating leverage would further strengthen an already attractive business model.

Government Platform Adoption Adds Strategic Value

Palantir's government business provides another source of long-term strength. Its Maven-related platform activity illustrates how deeply the company can become embedded within large operational programs.

More than 25,000 developers and participants have reportedly been building applications and AI agents around the platform. Although this should not be interpreted as paid-user data, the level of participation suggests that Palantir technology can become an operating environment on which additional tools and workflows are created.

That type of ecosystem can reinforce customer dependence on the underlying platform and expand its strategic importance over time.

Analyst Sentiment Remains Highly Favorable

Consensus estimates continue to support Palantir's growth trajectory. Earnings are projected to increase 114.7% in 2026 and 40% in 2027, while revenue growth expectations remain robust at 83% in 2026 and 42.5% in 2027.

Analyst sentiment has also improved considerably. Over the past 60 days, analysts issued 10 upward earnings estimate revisions for 2026 and none downward. Forecasts for 2027 also moved higher, with 10 upward revisions and none downward, reflecting growing confidence in Palantir's execution capabilities and expanding AI opportunity.

Valuation and Accounting Risks Should Not Be Ignored

Palantir's rapid appreciation means investors are paying heavily for future growth. A forward EV/EBITDA multiple around 66 times reflects expectations for sustained exceptional revenue growth, margin expansion and cash generation.

Stock-based compensation also remains meaningful. It totaled about $265 million in the latest quarter, equivalent to nearly 14% of revenues, creating ongoing dilution concerns.

Investors should also be cautious about extrapolating current net profitability. Palantir's unusually low effective tax rate contributed to reported earnings strength and may not represent a normalized long-term tax profile.

How Do Palantir's Peers Stack Up?

Microsoft MSFT remains one of the most important comparisons because of its expanding enterprise AI ecosystem and deep integration of AI tools into corporate software environments. Microsoft benefits from enormous distribution through Azure and its productivity applications. Still, Palantir differentiates itself by focusing heavily on linking AI directly with operational data and workflows. Microsoft remains a formidable competitor, but Palantir's specialized architecture could sustain demand in complex deployments where governance, integration and execution are critical.

Oracle ORCL is another relevant enterprise technology peer due to its extensive database, cloud infrastructure and business-application footprint. Oracle continues to expand its AI capabilities across enterprise systems, giving customers another pathway for integrating AI with critical corporate data. However, Palantir's emphasis on building operational digital environments across disparate systems provides a different value proposition. Oracle has considerable scale, while Palantir is increasingly positioning itself as a specialized operating layer for AI-enabled decision-making.

Why PLTR Looks Like a Buy

Palantir's investment case rests on more than rapid AI-related revenue growth. The company is becoming deeply embedded within critical customer operations, while expanding deployments suggest rising platform value after initial adoption. Its ability to connect artificial intelligence with governed enterprise workflows creates meaningful differentiation and potentially high switching costs. Improving deployment efficiency could broaden customer adoption, while government and commercial momentum provide multiple growth avenues. Valuation remains demanding and shareholder dilution deserves attention, but Palantir's expanding strategic importance, exceptional operating leverage and strengthening customer economics support continued upside. For investors comfortable with premium valuations, PLTR remains a Buy.

PLTR stock currently sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

news.Title: 1 Stat That Makes Amazon Hard to Ignore Right Now
news.Content:
As a massive enterprise with numerous segments, Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) provides investors with a lot of facts and figures they can use in the research process. But during the most recent quarter, one number stood out. Here's one stat that makes this Magnificent Seven stock hard to ignore right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

As of June 30, which was the end of the company's second quarter, Amazon Web Services (AWS) reported a massive customer backlog of $496 billion. This figure represented a notable increase from $364 billion just three months before. And it was up a triple-digit percentage from 12 months earlier.

This single metric reveals why Amazon's capital expenditures, like those of other hyperscalers, are ballooning. They are expected to total $220 billion this year. The dominant cloud computing platform is seeing incredible demand, boosted by interest in artificial intelligence (AI).

"Customers seeking the full benefits of AI are accelerating their transition to the cloud," Chief Financial Officer Brian Olsavsky said on the second quarter earnings call. This is driving revenue acceleration at AWS, with the top line rising last quarter at the fastest pace in 18 quarters.

However, investors should understand the level of customer concentration here. Earlier in 2026, Anthropic and OpenAI each signed $100 billion multi-year deals with AWS. These leading AI labs generate revenue that will fall significantly short of their spending plans in future years. That funding gap presents a risk for Amazon.

news.Title: Samsung May Report Its First 100 Trillion Won Quarter. Micron Stock Has More to Lose Than to Gain.
news.Content:
Samsung Electronics (OTC:SSNLF) will probably release its preliminary third-quarter results this week, and the number investors are waiting for is 100 trillion won. FnGuide's consensus for the company's quarterly operating profit was 106.94 trillion won as of Oct. 2.

This might top the record 89.5 trillion won Samsung made in the second quarter by around 19%. It may also be the first quarter in the company's history over 100 trillion won.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Brokers have been trimming the forecasts, though. But the cuts point mainly to a stronger Korean won, bonus costs, and losses at Samsung's phone unit -- not softer demand for memory chips.

And this matters for Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU). Samsung is one of Micron's two big memory rivals. Its numbers will be the first big outside look at memory pricing since Micron posted record results on Sept. 30 and forecast another record quarter. Micron shares trade near $1,075 as of this writing, about 14% under their 52-week high of $1,255.

Image source: Micron.

Slower price gains

Showing how much of Micron's boom comes from price, its DRAM revenue rose to a record $39.8 billion for fiscal Q4 2026 (a 14-week span ending Sept. 3), up 343% year over year and 27% sequentially. DRAM bit shipments grew by just a mid-single-digit percentage from the previous quarter. This was mostly driven by DRAM prices, which climbed by a percentage in the high teens. NAND prices rose about 30%. And Micron's non-GAAP (adjusted) gross margin hit 87%, up from 84.9% the quarter before and 74.9% the quarter before that.

But the high-teens price gain was a fraction of the one before it. In fiscal Q3, Micron's DRAM prices jumped by a percentage in the low 60s.

Management expects the slowdown to continue. Micron forecast record fiscal first-quarter revenue of around $61.5 billion, a 13% sequential rise. And because the fourth quarter was a week longer than normal, the weekly pace is faster still.

After this quarter, Micron sees higher gross margins for the rest of fiscal 2027 "with a more moderate rate of price increases," CFO Mark Murphy said in his remarks for the Sept. 30 call.

Put another way, Micron's guidance assumes memory prices keep rising, just more slowly.

What can Samsung's number show?

Samsung's preliminary report has just two figures, consolidated revenue and operating profit. Its July 7 guidance for the second quarter, for example, gave sales of around 171 trillion won and nothing on memory.

Story Continues

Still, I'd say the tech company's profit figure is mainly a memory number. Samsung's device solutions chip division earned 89.2 trillion won of the company's 89.5 trillion won second-quarter operating profit, and memory made up 120.8 trillion won of the division's 127.5 trillion won in sales.

But other things can cloud it. Samsung sells many of its chips in dollars and reports in won, so a stronger won shrinks the result. A Korean brokerage cut its exchange-rate assumption to 1,400 won per dollar from 1,440, a gap of about 3%.

Bonus provisions can raise costs, too. And Samsung's July-through-September quarter mainly overlaps the quarter Micron already reported, not the one it's guiding for now.

The division breakdown comes later. Samsung's second-quarter earnings call was on July 30, over three weeks after the quarter's guidance.

A big miss would matter more than a beat

IBK Securities, for one, cut its operating profit forecast by 12.8% to about 101.7 trillion won, citing the won and bonuses carried over from the second quarter. A result a few trillion won below consensus, then, could easily come down to currency and pay, not prices.

A number back near the second quarter's 89.5 trillion won would be tougher to explain away. With price driving most of Micron's growth, flat profit for Samsung might suggest memory prices stalled in late summer, right as Micron's current quarter started.

Samsung said in July that it expected spending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure to keep the memory market "undersupplied" in the second half. A figure around consensus would largely confirm that, and it may support the pricing behind Micron's guidance.

But I don't think a strong number does much for Micron stock. Micron's fiscal 2026 earnings under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) were $74.33 per share, so the stock trades at around 14 times earnings. That's a price for profits investors expect to fade, and a Samsung beat likely won't change that. A miss that the won and bonuses can't explain is another matter. That result is the one I'd watch for this week.

即使到了比賽期間，營養師也持續提供飲食上的建議，包括賽後增加蛋白質、適量補充水果，協助身體恢復。為了控制體重，林郁婷也得忍住對零食、洋芋片等食物的喜愛，一路堅持到亞運，最終用金牌替這段過程畫下句點。

來自粉絲的支持也是林郁婷走過低潮的重要力量。她透露，不論比賽輸贏或表現好壞，都會收到粉絲透過手寫卡片、訊息傳來的鼓勵，讓她在遇到挫折時感受到支持。

即使外界仍有不同聲音，支持她的粉絲始終沒有離開，「非常感謝他們，讓我可以治癒自己，在比賽前重新站起來。」林郁婷表示，正是這些陪伴，讓她能重新整理好自己，再次投入比賽。

news.Title: Why SpaceX Stock Took Flight Today
news.Content:
Shares of Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX), aka SpaceX, took flight early on Monday, climbing as much as 6.4% in early trading. As of 11:47 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 4.9%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Two catalysts sent the space stock higher: Bullish commentary from a Wall Street analyst and the potential for an exclusive deal with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM), commonly called TSMC.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

On a roll

Kicking off the week on a positive note, Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas maintained his overweight (buy) rating and reiterated his $300 price target on SpaceX. For those keeping score at home, that suggests potential upside of 89% compared to Friday's closing price. The analyst goes on to say that the stock is "cheap and getting cheaper" when viewed in the context of its growth, despite its otherwise lofty valuation.

Dividing SpaceX's 2028 estimated enterprise value by its earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) yields a multiple of 30, making it appear nearly twice as expensive as a basket of mega-cap artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, according to the analyst. However, factoring in the company's growth yields a valuation of 0.3, lower than the multiple of 0.5 for the AI-centric basket, which includes Amazon , Alphabet , and Meta Platforms . The analyst posits that investors are underestimating the growth potential of SpaceX's xAI segment.

Also fueling today's gains was confirmation from SpaceX CEO Elon Musk that talks with TSMC are ongoing regarding a potential partnership. If it were to come to fruition, TSMC would build and operate a semiconductor manufacturing facility that would supply chips exclusively to Tesla , SpaceX, and xAI. Musk noted that while it's "Just discussions, but something may come of it."

It's easy to see why investors are excited. That said, it's also important to remember that, despite the potential, SpaceX will still have to execute on its vision for AI data centers in space -- which is by no means a given.

為了順利維持60公斤級體重，林郁婷今年也在飲食管理上做出更細緻的調整，特別感謝國訓中心營養師曾怡鈞。她表示，過去主要依照營養師提供的建議自行評估，今年則改以每餐裝好餐盤後拍照的方式，讓營養師根據熱量需求、訓練量及身體恢復狀況協助調整份量。

即使到了比賽期間，營養師也持續提供飲食上的建議，包括賽後增加蛋白質、適量補充水果，協助身體恢復。為了控制體重，林郁婷也得忍住對零食、洋芋片等食物的喜愛，一路堅持到亞運，最終用金牌替這段過程畫下句點。

來自粉絲的支持也是林郁婷走過低潮的重要力量。她透露，不論比賽輸贏或表現好壞，都會收到粉絲透過手寫卡片、訊息傳來的鼓勵，讓她在遇到挫折時感受到支持。

即使外界仍有不同聲音，支持她的粉絲始終沒有離開，「非常感謝他們，讓我可以治癒自己，在比賽前重新站起來。」林郁婷表示，正是這些陪伴，讓她能重新整理好自己，再次投入比賽。

宏道運動發展基金會選手本屆亞運共拿下2金3銀8銅，林郁婷則以女子拳擊60公斤級金牌完成亞運二連霸，也替台灣拳擊使締造新猷。

news.Title: Amazon stock is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, despite AI boom
news.Content:
Amazon ( AMZN ) is being left out of the renewed interest in owning AI stocks.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) is trading at a record high . Rival AMD ( AMD ) just hit a record high . Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Google ( GOOG ) have tacked on modest gains in the past month. Meta ( META ) shares have surged 23% on Muse AI agent fever .

Contrast those gains with Amazon, which is down 2.4% over the past month. In fact, at its current stock price of $251 and trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 20x, Amazon is trading at its lowest valuation ever as a public company, the team at TrendSpider pointed out.

Amazon has the second-lowest trailing P/E ratio among the "Magnificent Seven" names. Only Alphabet trails, at 17.7 times forward earnings, per Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data .

There are a couple of factors likely holding Amazon stock back right now.

For starters, in early September, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 22 states filed a lawsuit alleging that Amazon's advertising practices have overcharged its roughly 1.2 million advertisers by $20 billion from 2019 to the present.

The FTC contended Amazon didn't disclose reserve-pricing mechanisms that ultimately increased costs for advertisers and consumers.

Amazon responded by saying advertisers are receiving greater value from its platform.

Whatever the case, investors are taking a wait-and-see approach to Amazon shares, fearing that a lucrative profit center for Amazon — advertising — may become less lucrative in the future.

Lingering concerns about how much Big Tech is spending on AI infrastructure are also not helping Amazon's stock.

Dive deeper into Big Tech's AI spending plans:

Big Tech is about to spend trillions to dominate the AI era

Tech's AI debt boom, in one chart

Google raises capex growth expectations again

Recall that in its second quarter earnings release, Amazon announced it is significantly expanding its full-year 2026 capital expenditures budget to approximately $220 billion.

And the aggressive spending is poised to continue, Wall Street says.

"We now estimate Amazon's 2027 capex to be $320 billion, and its 2028 capex to be $370 billion. Accordingly, we now estimate negative free cash flow in 2027 and 2028 of approximately -$50 billion in each year," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney warned.
