news.Title: Alphabet Rides on Google Services Growth: Can It Beat META & AAPL?
news.Content:
Alphabet GOOGL is benefiting from strong momentum across Google Services, supported by robust Search, YouTube, and subscription growth. This strengthens the company's competitive position against Meta Platforms META and Apple AAPL.

In the second quarter of 2026, Google Services revenues increased 15% year over year to $94.5 billion, driven by 17% growth in Google Search & other, 15% growth in subscriptions, platforms and devices and 13% growth in YouTube advertising revenues. Google Services operating income also rose 20% to $39.5 billion, with margin reaching 41.8%, highlighting solid profitability alongside revenue expansion.

AI integration is strengthening Search engagement and monetization. In the second quarter of 2026, AI Mode has surpassed 1 billion monthly active users and is driving incremental Search queries. Gemini is also being integrated across the advertising infrastructure to improve query understanding and ad relevance. Advertisers using AI-powered campaigns such as AI Max or Performance Max are seeing an average 15% increase in conversions or conversion value at a similar return on ad spend.

YouTube is another key growth driver. Advertising revenues increased 13% to $11.1 billion, while YouTube Music and Premium supported strong subscription growth. Google subscriptions, platforms and devices revenues increased 15% to $12.91 billion, aided by Google One and demand for AI plans.

Continued AI integration across Search, YouTube and subscriptions should support Google Services growth and help Alphabet strengthen its competitive standing against Meta Platforms and Apple. Management expects Google Services to continue benefiting from AI-driven improvements to the user and advertiser experience in the second half of 2026.

How Competitors Fare Against GOOGL

Meta Platforms is challenging Alphabet through its AI-powered recommendations and advertising tools across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads. Its massive user base and AI-driven ad infrastructure make it a major rival to Alphabet for digital advertising budgets and consumer engagement.

In the second quarter of 2026, Meta Platforms' advertising revenues increased 27% year over year to $59.4 billion. AI-powered recommendations and ad-ranking enhancements are improving advertiser performance, while Advantage+ solutions surpassed a $75 billion annual revenue run rate. With 3.6 billion daily users across its apps, Meta Platforms offers advertisers substantial reach.

Apple competes with Alphabet across subscriptions, digital content and consumer AI. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Apple's services revenues reached a record of $30.7 billion, up 12% year over year, led by records across cloud, payments, advertising, App Store and video. Paid subscriptions surpassed 1.5 billion, supported by record transacting and paid accounts. Privacy-focused AI is also expected to become a new Services growth driver as heavy AI users may eventually upgrade to higher-tier iCloud+ subscriptions to support expanded compute needs.

news.Title: TSMC (TSM) is a Great Momentum Stock: Should You Buy?
news.Content:
Momentum investing revolves around the idea of following a stock's recent trend in either direction. In "long context," investors will be essentially be "buying high, but hoping to sell even higher." With this methodology, taking advantage of trends in a stock's price is key; once a stock establishes a course, it is more than likely to continue moving that way. The goal is that once a stock heads down a fixed path, it will lead to timely and profitable trades.

Even though momentum is a popular stock characteristic, it can be tough to define. Debate surrounding which are the best and worst metrics to focus on is lengthy, but the Zacks Momentum Style Score, part of the Zacks Style Scores, helps address this issue for us.

Below, we take a look at TSMC (TSM) , which currently has a Momentum Style Score of B. We also discuss some of the main drivers of the Momentum Style Score, like price change and earnings estimate revisions.

It's also important to note that Style Scores work as a complement to the Zacks Rank, our stock rating system that has an impressive track record of outperformance. TSMC currently has a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy). Our research shows that stocks rated Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and #2 (Buy) and Style Scores of "A or B" outperform the market over the following one-month period.

You can see the current list of Zacks #1 Rank Stocks here >>>

Set to Beat the Market?

In order to see if TSM is a promising momentum pick, let's examine some Momentum Style elements to see if this chip company holds up.

Looking at a stock's short-term price activity is a great way to gauge if it has momentum, since this can reflect both the current interest in a stock and if buyers or sellers have the upper hand at the moment. It is also useful to compare a security to its industry, as this can help investors pinpoint the top companies in a particular area.

For TSM, shares are up 3.67% over the past week while the Zacks Semiconductor - Circuit Foundry industry is up 3.67% over the same time period. Shares are looking quite well from a longer time frame too, as the monthly price change of 10.37% compares favorably with the industry's 10.37% performance as well.

Considering longer term price metrics, like performance over the last three months or year, can be advantageous as well. Over the past quarter, shares of TSMC have risen 5.63%, and are up 63.61% in the last year. In comparison, the S&P 500 has only moved 3.43% and 16.37%, respectively.

Investors should also pay attention to TSM's average 20-day trading volume. Volume is a useful item in many ways, and the 20-day average establishes a good price-to-volume baseline; a rising stock with above average volume is generally a bullish sign, whereas a declining stock on above average volume is typically bearish. TSM is currently averaging 9,514,646 shares for the last 20 days.

Story Continues

Earnings Outlook

The Zacks Momentum Style Score also takes into account trends in estimate revisions, in addition to price changes. Please note that estimate revision trends remain at the core of Zacks Rank as well. A nice path here can help show promise, and we have recently been seeing that with TSM.

Over the past two months, 2 earnings estimates moved higher compared to none lower for the full year. These revisions helped boost TSM's consensus estimate, increasing from $16.45 to $16.56 in the past 60 days. Looking at the next fiscal year, 2 estimates have moved upwards while there have been no downward revisions in the same time period.

Bottom Line

Taking into account all of these elements, it should come as no surprise that TSM is a #2 (Buy) stock with a Momentum Score of B. If you've been searching for a fresh pick that's set to rise in the near-term, make sure to keep TSMC on your short list.

news.Content:

TSMC is evaluating a potential investment in Texas to expand chip production in the United States, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing two people familiar with the matter. The plans have not been finalized, the sources said.

Any Texas investment would come in addition to the $265 billion TSMC has already committed to Arizona, according to one of the sources.

That makes the potential expansion particularly notable for investors. TSMC isn't considering Texas instead of its existing U.S. manufacturing plans. It could represent another layer on top of what is already one of the semiconductor industry's largest manufacturing investments.

TSMC expanded its Arizona commitment by another $100 billion in July, bringing the total planned investment in the state to $265 billion.

CEO C.C. Wei said at the time that the company would probably build another four or more fabs, including front-end and back-end facilities.

Including existing and planned projects, TSMC's Arizona operation is expected to encompass 12 fabrication and advanced packaging facilities as well as an R&D center.

The company has also previously indicated that its U.S. investment may not stop there. Chief Financial Officer Wendell Huang told Reuters in July that TSMC would continue investing in the United States.

TSMC did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment on the potential Texas project. For now, Texas remains an evaluation rather than a committed expansion. But if TSMC moves forward, it would extend a U.S. manufacturing footprint that is already growing far beyond the company's original Arizona plans.

news.Title: Will CoWoS & Panel Packaging Demand Drive ASX's Next Growth Phase?
news.Content:
ASE Technology Holding ASX is expanding its advanced packaging capabilities as AI drives demand for larger chips, higher bandwidth and more complex semiconductor designs. Rising AI demand is creating hardware requirements in terms of size, complexity and integration, making packaging an important part of the AI infrastructure buildout. ASE Technology believes that hardware infrastructure has become a key bottleneck, while packaging is moving up in the system architecture value chain.

CoWoS is one of the main technologies supporting this opportunity. The company is working to increase its CoWoS scale and efficiency as demand from AI infrastructure remains strong. ASE Technology is also expanding its full process business, which management said is on track to generate about TWD 300 million in revenues in 2026. The company expects substantial growth in this business in 2027 and sees it becoming margin accretive as it scales.

Panel-level packaging could add another growth opportunity. ASX's fully-automated 310-by-310 panel line is expected to start production in the first quarter of 2027. Management said that the solution is complementary to foundry offerings and is aimed at a similar customer set and reticle size. Customer adoption will depend on factors such as capacity, performance and speed of execution. This gives ASE Technology another packaging option as customers look for solutions to meet rising AI hardware requirements.

The growth opportunity is supported by ASX's broader LEAP business. First-half 2026 consolidated revenues increased 24% year over year, while ATM revenues grew 35%. Management expects full-year ATM revenues to increase 35%, with LEAP service revenues tracking ahead of its earlier $3.5-billion target. ASE Technology also aims to double LEAP revenues in 2027 as it adds facilities and equipment. If ASX can bring the new capacity online as planned, CoWoS, panel packaging and LEAP could provide multiple growth drivers as AI infrastructure demand continues to expand.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 and 2027 indicates year-over-year revenue growth of 27.9% and 22.5%, respectively.

Here's How Competitors Fare Against ASE Technology

ASX faces stiff competition from the likes of Amkor Technology AMKR and Intel INTC in advanced semiconductor packaging.

Amkor Technology is expanding its advanced packaging business as demand from AI and high-performance computing remains strong. In the second quarter, Amkor reported record revenues of $1.9 billion, rising 26% year over year. Management said that growth was supported by advanced packaging and demand across its end markets. Amkor is also expanding its strategic relationships with TSMC and NVIDIA to support advanced packaging and AI infrastructure.

Story Continues

Intel is investing heavily in advanced packaging as AI demand increases the need for more computing capacity. Intel said that customer interest in its EMIB-T packaging technology remains high, with a growing backlog and plans to ramp the technology into high-volume production in 2027. The company also raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to more than $20 billion and expects 2027 spending to be significantly higher, with the majority of the investment going toward its U.S. network.

For fiscal 2027, Jabil expects Regulated Industries revenues of $13.6 billion, up 7%. Management sees growth across all three end markets, including a 9% increase in Automotive and Transportation, 6% growth in Healthcare and Packaging and a 7% rise in Renewable and Energy Infrastructure.

news.Title: How to Play QCOM Stock as Apple Renews Licensing Agreement With Qualcomm
news.Content:
Qualcomm (QCOM) recently announced that Apple (AAPL) has renewed its licensing agreement with the company. Not revealing much about the contours of the deal, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing John Han said, "We are pleased to extend the Apple license agreement."

Apple and Qualcomm have had a longstanding partnership over the years, wherein the latter supplied the former with modem chips, while Qualcomm also earned royalty revenues from Apple. However, since Apple acquired Intel's (INTC) modem business in 2019 for about $1 billion, its dependence on Qualcomm has been decreasing.

More News from Barchart

At one point, Apple sued Qualcomm for its supposedly excessive royalties. The suit was settled in 2019, and one of the points of settlement included a six-year global patent licensing agreement, effective April 1, 2019. This is the agreement that has been renewed and will be effective as of April 1, 2027.

About Qualcomm

Founded in 1985, Qualcomm is both a semiconductor company and an intellectual-property/licensing company. Its historical strength comes from inventing foundational wireless technologies and licensing them broadly, while its current strategy is to use that technology base to expand from smartphones into other areas.

Valued at a market capitalization of $197 billion, QCOM stock is up 8% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. The stock also offers a dividend yield of 1.82%, with the company on the verge of becoming a "Dividend Aristocrat," having raised its dividend for the past 23 consecutive years.

So, Qualcomm hasn't been on fire. But does that make it a sound investment now? Let's take a closer look.

A Stealthy Start

When Qualcomm announced that it was reentering the data-center business, the market reacted positively. Shares popped as investors believed that the competitive intensity in the chip business would increase to challenge the hegemony of Nvidia (NVDA), and AMD (AMD) to a lesser extent. Yet after the initial pop, Qualcomm's share price performance has been sedated, to say the least. That's despite the company signing agreements with the likes of Meta Platforms (META), Amazon (AMZN) and Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN.

Story Continues

Why is Qualcomm ailing? Well, one of the reasons seems to be just plain bad luck. Qualcomm's core business is still handsets, and the sharp rise in memory prices has coincided with the company's AI ambitions — both of which require substantial memory infrastructure. Moreover, as mentioned earlier, Apple building its own modems has not helped matters for the company.

Qualcomm has ambitions to reach $15 billion in data-center revenue by fiscal 2029, and its recent deals with hyperscalers should certainly help. Having said that, funding a data-center business from scratch is an arduous task and dilutive to a company's margins. If a company's core business — like handset revenues for Qualcomm — takes a hit at the same time, the scenario becomes even more grim.

Things could change next year with Dragonfly, the company's data-center infrastructure platform encompassing AI accelerators, server CPUs, high-speed connectivity, and software with a particular focus on energy-efficient, rack-scale AI inference. Its speciality is framed around a tightly integrated compute stack that blends a dedicated AI core with general-purpose processing and a high-bandwidth memory (HBM) fabric so workloads can be moved between fast local compute and broader server resources without friction. In addition, Dragonfly is built to work with Qualcomm's broader ecosystem, which includes 5G network and edge-compute platforms so operators can push intelligence closer to customers while preserving centralized control and governance.

Finally, Qualcomm claims up to 8 times better tokens per second per watt than comparable GPU-based systems, more than 2 times better performance per watt than contemporary server CPUs, and 6 times higher memory bandwidth per watt than conventional HBM-based designs. Its High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) architecture places compute close to memory, reducing energy-intensive data movement, and is claimed to provide up to 200 times greater memory capacity per watt than SRAM-based approaches.

Qualcomm Reports a Mixed Q3

Qualcomm's latest results for the third quarter of fiscal 2026 were marked by a decline in both revenue and earnings. However, revenue at least managed to surpass Wall Street estimates, as high memory prices hurt overall operations.

Qualcomm's revenue fell 4% year-over-year (YOY) to $9.9 billion, as the key handset segment saw a sharp drop of 20% YOY to $5.1 billion. The decline in Q3 licensing revenue was not as acute, but it fell nonetheless. Coming in at $1.3 billion, licensing revenue was down 3% YOY. Meanwhile, non-GAAP diluted EPS fell 20% YOY to $2.21, missing the consensus estimate of $2.23 per share.

For Q4, Qualcomm expects EPS to be between $2.05 and $2.25. The midpoint of that guidance denotes an expected decline of 28% YOY from $3 per share in Q4 2025. In terms of sales, Qualcomm expects chips revenue to range between $8.4 billion and $9 billion and licensing revenue to range between $1.2 billion and $1.4 billion.

Notably, Q3 also saw gross margins correcting to 53% from 56% in the year-ago period. Further, net cash from operating activities for the nine months ended June 28, 2026 was $8.4 billion, down from $10 billion in the prior-year period. Overall, Qualcomm ended the quarter with a cash balance of $4.5 billion, higher than its short-term debt levels of roughly $2.5 billion.

Qualcomm's muted stock price performance this year has brought its valuation multiples to relatively reasonable levels, however. While its price-to-cash flow (P/CF) ratio of 17 times is below the sector median, the forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 26 times and the forward price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 4.7 times are both above the sector medians of 23 times and 3.4 times, respectively.

What Do Analysts Think of Qualcomm Stock?

Overall, analysts have a consensus "Hold" rating for QCOM stock. Out of 33 analysts covering the stock, nine have a "Strong Buy" rating, two have a "Moderate Buy" rating, 18 have a "Hold" rating, one has a "Moderate Sell" rating, and three have a "Strong Sell" rating.

The mean target price of $198.31 indicates potential upside of 8% from current levels. Meanwhile, the high target price of $400 denotes potential upside of about 117% from here.

news.Title: SCHMID Sizzles on Possible Use of Glass Substrates by Chipmakers. How to Play SHMD Stock Here.
news.Content:
Irrespective of where oil prices or bond yields are heading. Irrespective of the safety concerns and the supposed sage advice from the industry leaders to slow down. Artificial intelligence remains the "it" thing on Wall Street, and mere mention of any connection with the revolutionary tech is enough to send a company's stock on a searing rally.

That is what happened with SCHMID (SHMD), the German industrial tech company. Shares popped more than 20% last week on Friday after reports emerged that chip giants, such as Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD), and Intel (INTC), are considering the use of glass substrates.

More News from Barchart

Warren Buffett Says America Is Doing Something 'Unsustainable' and Doesn't Know If We Have 2 Years or 20 —'This Can't Go On Forever'

'It's Your Only Option' — Late Billionaire Charlie Munger, 99, Shared His Iron Rule for Overcoming Life's Hardship. 'Everybody Struggles, But You Can't Quit'

Rocket Lab Steps In Where SpaceX Just Walked Away

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

In the company's Q2 earnings call, Roland Rettenmaier, the company's Chief Sales Officer, said, "A lot of players in the Intel supply chain, in the Nvidia supply chain, AMD supply chain, you name them, are putting an eye on glass core substrates, in terms of its flatness, its smoothness, in terms of diverse constants like dielectric constants and signal integrity. So we are engaged with most of the major of the supply chain players, and we are supporting them with our technology and equipment to make glass core substrates real."

About SCHMID

Founded in 1864, SCHMID develops and manufactures specialized equipment, software, and process solutions used in producing printed circuit boards (PCBs), semiconductor substrates, advanced packaging components, photovoltaic products, glass, and energy-storage systems. The company primarily sells the specialized machinery and process technologies that manufacturers use to produce complex electronic components.

Valued at a market cap of $252.6 million, SHMD stock is down 29.4% YTD.

So, can SCHMID's faltering stock stage a turnaround on this development? Let's find out.

Feeding Glass Substrates

To set the record straight, SCHMID does not manufacture glass substrates itself. It develops and supplies the process technology and specialized equipment that substrate manufacturers use to produce them. Moreover, the company itself describes its glass-substrate activity as being focused on R&D, pilot lines, and early engagement with original-equipment manufacturers, with volume adoption expected over the medium to long term.

Story Continues

In fact, one of its potential customers is a notable glass substrate manufacturer. Intel is one of the most prominent technology developers in glass-core substrates, having publicly demonstrated test substrates and outlined potential advantages over conventional organic materials. Its research highlights include better dimensional stability, reduced warpage, improved signal integrity, and the possibility of fitting more dies into a given substrate area.

So, how can SCHMID take advantage of the potential rise in demand for glass substrates? Here, SCHMID's expertise in wet chemical processing, plasma etching, chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP), automation, and large-panel handling can serve it well. Then, one of SCHMID's key offerings is its InfinityLine L+ full-panel CMP system, which is designed to polish and planarize large substrate panels. CMP is important because advanced packaging requires highly uniform surfaces for subsequent layer formation and bonding.

Further, its proprietary Embedded Trace (ET) process is another part of its differentiation. It forms copper traces within dielectric material rather than simply placing patterned copper on the surface. SCHMID says this approach can enable finer structures, improved planarity, and more flexible 3D interconnect designs.

SCHMID's Finances Sigh

The excitement around SCHMID may turn into something concrete in the future. However, for now, the company's finances do not evoke much excitement.

Although revenues for the first six months of 2026 surged to 46 million euros from 16.9 million euros in the same period last year, net losses widened to 47.8 million euros from 10.2 million euros in the year-ago period. Yet, the widening of losses cannot be fully attributed to operating issues, as a conversion of liability into company shares contributed to the losses.

Having said that, order momentum is gaining, as sharp sequential growth was witnessed in the same period this year. While order intake was just 13.6 million euros in the first quarter, it accelerated to 30.7 million euros and 52.3 million euros in Q2 and Q3 (through August 21), respectively. The company also raised its order intake guidance for 2026 to 125 million to 150 million euros from 114 million euros earlier.

Cash flow from operating activities continued to remain negative at 29.3 million euros for H1 2026, as SCHMID ended the period with a cash balance of 2.3 million euros. This was much lower than its short-term debt levels of about 40 million euros.

Concluding Take

SCHMID has talked about how glass substrates can be a potential game-changer for the company, and murmurs from the top players of its usage for their chips have sent SCHMID shares soaring. Moreover, SCHMID has some technological advantages and expertise in building the manufacturing prowess that is required for glass substrate production. Yet, that is all mere speculation now. One should at least wait for the next earnings call, where the management should provide more color regarding capacity, the proportion of orders attributed to glass substrate, and any key customer wins on this front.

Finally, all this has to be built in a manner that is financially viable, as the company's finances are already under strain. Navigating through all of these issues will be a difficult task, and only when the company can signal strongly that it is able to do that can an investment in the stock be considered. However, for now, I would give SCHMID a pass.

news.Title: 《陸股》滬指漲0.31%、日K連二紅；科創50跌2.51%
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-09-30 17:23:47 數位內容中心 發佈

中國A股今(30)日收盤漲跌不一，上證指數收於3842.19點，上漲11.74點或0.31%，日K連二紅；深證成指收於12887.62點，下跌14.33點或0.11%；創業板指收於3135.28點，下跌7.28點或0.23%；科創50收於1530.01點，下跌39.33點或2.51%，在主要指數中表現最弱。整體盤勢仍以震盪整理為主，長假前交投偏謹慎，資金輪動明顯。

以月線來看，上證指數本月跌3.62%、月K翻黑，深證成指跌8.04%、創業板指跌8.82%。成交量方面，滬市今成交6,794億元(人民幣,下同)，深市成交7,586億元，兩市成交額1兆4,380億元，較前一交易日量增約2%。

依盤面上來看，半導體、電子元件與部分AI硬體概念同步回檔，芯原股份、康強電子、寒武紀、瀾起科技等承壓，科技成長族群走勢偏弱。

相較之下，醫藥生物、創新藥與CRO族群表現突出，盤中維持活躍，部分個股一度漲停。市場資金明顯偏向醫藥主線，帶動相關類股成為今日盤勢中最具支撐力的方向之一。

此外，房地產類股早盤一度承壓，隨後探底回升，深物業A、萬科A等個股表現轉強，陸家嘴、中天服務等也跟進走揚。銀行股同樣偏強，顯示防禦型與低檔族群獲得資金青睞。

news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉製造業PMI重返擴張區間 三大指數漲跌互見
news.Content:
中國A股三大指數周三（30日）收盤漲跌互見，中國製造業活動自6月以來首次恢復擴張，隨著政策制定者推出新措施支持經濟發展，為第三季畫下了亮眼句點。

上證指數周三收報3,842.19點，漲0.31%。深證成指收報12,887.62點，跌0.11%。創業板指收報3,135.28點，跌0.23%。

中國國家統計局周三公布的數據顯示，9月官方製造業採購經理人指數（PMI）為 50.1，高於8月的 49.8，符合經濟學家預測。

涵蓋建築業與服務業的非製造業活動指數意外重返擴張區間，達到 50.2。指數高於 50 即代表產業活動擴張。

這些數據是在中國政府啟動兩年來最大規模刺激方案數小時後公布；在上季經濟成長速度降至 4.5% 至 5% 的年度目標區間以下後，此舉大幅提升中國實現全年成長目標的可能性。

儘管出口表現具韌性，且人工智慧（AI）帶動工業利潤成長，中國經濟仍持續承壓。消費成長已放緩至接近零的水準，企業信心依然低迷，投資亦持續萎縮。

即便如此，在美中兩國同意將貿易休戰期限延長兩個月、減少了短期貿易不確定性之後，中國的外部環境已適度轉好。

news.Title: AI交易大退潮！韓股Q3暴跌18.8%  但今年來累漲60%仍勝標普2.3%漲幅
news.Content:
今年第三季(9月30日止)，南韓股市遭遇劇烈反轉，綜合股指(Kospi)暴跌18.8%，成為同期全球表現最差的主要股市之一，這場拋售潮發生在AI交易突然逆轉之後，此前押注AI基礎設施需求的熱門標的三星電子和SK海力士等記憶體晶片股成重災區。儘管如此，Kospi今年來仍累計上漲60%，表現位居全球前列。相比之下，標普500指數同期僅上漲2.3%。

法國巴黎銀行財富管理公司亞洲首席投資長Prashant Bhayani表示，南韓市場已成為投資者判斷AI基設巨額資本支出前景的重要代理指標，7月的劇烈平倉是本輪調整的關鍵轉捩點。

避險基金Situational Awareness創辦人Leopold Aschenbrenner先前對南韓記憶體晶片股持有大規模槓桿部位，其部位崩盤與散戶大量買入槓桿單一股票ETF同時發生，進一步放大市場波動。

進入Q3季底，新的壓力來自債市。全球公債殖利率持續走高，威脅韓股自2025年初以來逾185%的累積漲幅。法國里昂證券韓國研究主管沈鐘民說：「我確實認為債市將拖累股市，這是全球性的現象。」

Bhayani則說，7月拋售後估值已更具吸引力，但大幅估值擴張空間有限，「我們可能看到合理回報，但會看到70%？不可能。」

目前，SK海力士和三星電子的遠期本益比已降至4至5倍區間，兩家公司合計約佔韓股市值的一半。

Robeco亞太股票主管Joshua Crabb表示，更高的債券殖利率構成「逆風」，但晶片股已使用低個位數本益比交易，直接影響有限。不過，標普全球市場情報8月報告警告，市場對「週期性供應過剩風險」的擔憂可能給未來獲利帶來壓力。

南韓利率環境也在變動，該國央行正升息以壓制過熱經濟中的通膨，此前房價和股市均明顯上漲。沈鐘民認為，利率上升可能進一步拖累回報。

儘管宏觀環境轉弱，AI支出仍是晶片股的核心支撐。沈鐘民看好南韓晶片商，稱美國大型雲端運算企業將繼續增加資本支出，「AI公司別無選擇。它們必須花錢，這是生死攸關的事。」HBM是輝達AI晶片的關鍵零組件，三星和SK海力士主導該市場，傳統DRAM和NAND價格大漲也為獲利提供額外支撐。

另一方面，公司治理風險引發市場警覺。《彭博資訊》報導指出，《大賣空》原型Michael Burry的門徒、Pomerium Capital創辦人Phil Clifton在週二(29日)的信中警告，投資韓國必須「特別程度的謹慎」。

他指出，韓股中看似充滿高成長、健康利潤率的企業，但股東與管理階層利益常錯置。由於遺產與贈與稅高達60%，控股家族有動機壓低股價、囤積現金、不付股息，使股票淪為「沒有票息的永久債券」，少數股東難以觸及超額價值。儘管南韓政府推動財閥治理改革，Clifton更看好日本市場，認為日本交易所的改革已相當成功，估價折價尚未完全消失。

AI退潮後，韓股正經歷估值與宏觀壓力的雙重考驗，而少數股東保護問題仍是長期隱憂。

news.Title: 百萬獎金入帳！華邦電被挖「超佛心歷史」網讚：準備跳槽過去
news.Content:
一名自稱華邦電員工的網友在Threads分享，第二季單季獎金最高達100萬元，預估工程師全年薪資可上看512萬元，貼文曝光後讓業界同仁羨煞不已，不少網友直呼「難怪學長都不離開」、「準備跳槽過去」

受惠於AI需求帶動的記憶體缺貨潮，多家台廠記憶體營收都呈現爆炸式成長，而記憶體大廠多以當季獲利回頭分紅，本季華邦電營業利益高達300億元，若以一成獲利回饋員工，約莫4000名員工分配綽綽有餘。

原PO在貼文表示，「哇靠，太扯，偉大的華邦電，這一季季獎金100萬啊，一年的年薪14個月加上4季季獎金，且不含加班部分，用底薪很粗略計算8萬元，8乘上14加上400共計512萬元年薪」，令他感嘆簡直是「躺著數錢」。貼文曝光後，不少網友直呼，「偉大的華邦電，這季獎金太扯了！」更有網友幽默表示「該跳槽去華邦電了」。

也有網友在Dcard討論，華邦電在景氣低谷時雖不發分紅，卻堅持不裁員，待景氣回溫便大方補償、重賞員工，展現「願意共體時艱的良心企業」形象，「工作那麼多年，第一次聽到有公司會上修獎金比例」、「是最公正的台灣公司，分紅甚至直接公開遊戲規則」

也有內行網友表示，「以前聽老前輩講過，邦邦在最慘的時候，大概就是叫大家多關一點燈，部門的每一分錢都要斤斤計較，但沒在把人拋下的」。更多留言稱在華邦電為「低調又佛心的公司」、「難怪在華邦電的學長都不離開」、「準備跳槽過去」。

（封面圖／東森新聞）

news.Title: 日經指數週三飆1.94%，軟銀、三菱日聯金融集團、東京威力科創股價亮眼
news.Content:
【財訊快報／劉敏夫】日本股市週三走升，主要受美國科技股週二走高所提振，且原油價格在經歷一週多來的最大跌幅後穩定下來，也有助於平撫市場情緒。收盤時，東證第一部指數上漲67.52點或1.67%，報4,108.65點；日經225指數則是上揚1,272.48點或1.94%，報66,753.75點。

受費城半導體指數週二收漲1.32%的提振，人工智能和晶片相關股票走高。原油期貨價格走低也為股票提供了額外支撐，因為供應擔憂的舒緩抑制了能源價格的上漲。

大和資產管理首席策略分析師Kazunori Tatebe表示，費城半導體指數的上漲是一個利多因素。儘管如此，國內外高漲的殖利率仍然是不利因素。在利率真正穩定下來之前，股市很難平穩、持續上漲。

週期性類股和價值型類股也出現上漲，早盤買盤主要集中在貸款機構和機械製造商類股。服務業和零售業股票表現落後。

儘管日股上揚，但是經濟數據捎來令人擔心的消息，日本週三公布的最新經濟數據顯示，日本8月工業產出初值月減1.70%，與市場預期月增1.40%呈現明顯落差，且降幅較前月的0.20%擴大，連續第二個月下滑。同時，日本8月零售銷售月減1.20%，略遜於市場預期的月減1.10%，並由前月的月增2.40%轉為下滑，顯示零售銷售在7月回升後出現回落。

個股表現方面，專注於投資高科技領域的軟銀集團股價上漲6.55%；半導體製程設備生產商東京威力科創股價上揚2.69%；營收逾三成來自北美市場的汽車製造大廠豐田汽車股價揚升1.34%；金融控股業者三菱日聯金融集團股價上升3.01%；能源開採商國際石油開發帝石股價則是滑落0.11%。

news.Title: 擴NOR布局，華邦電攜Spansion雙軌拓市
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-09-30 13:30:01 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電（2344）收購英飛凌NOR Flash及F-RAM事業案持續推進，而Spansion NOR Flash產品近期也取得信驊（5274）第8代 AST2700 BMC平台採用並通過驗證，新增AI伺服器應用切入點，雖然目前在BMC領域可能尚無顯著營收貢獻，主要市場仍以車用為主，不過仍可視為後續拓展伺服器市場的助力。

不過其產品線的客戶認證通常涉及產品、製程及生產工廠，企業所有權改變後，原有認證不一定直接移轉，部分客戶及商務合約仍須重新確認。不過目前產業環境，產能就是話語權，此次交易除了擴充產品及客戶布局，能取得多少穩定產能也是後續整合的重要環節。

華邦電指出，此次收購後，雙方NOR Flash業務不會直接合併發展，兄弟登山、各自努力的方式，被收購事業將維持既有品牌及商業模式獨立運作，華邦原有NOR Flash產品及長期發展規畫也不受影響，雙方各自在既有客戶及產品基礎上拓展市場。

Spansion在車用領域的長期佈局才是主要市場。英飛凌相關NOR Flash事業在車用市場已有客戶及認證基礎，交易完成後，雙方在車用市場可望形成互補。

news.Title: 華邦電Si-Cap合約能見度高，明年貢獻逐步提升
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-09-30 13:17:42 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電（2344）持續擴充矽電容（Si-Cap）產品布局，現有產能已有訂單支撐，今年進入量產後，隨既有產能逐步滿載，若要承接更多客戶需求，仍需增加產能。公司已投入約40億元建置專用Si-Cap產線，新機台產能開出後，Si-Cap明年營收占比雖然仍小，但也有5%至10%的營收比重，有助調整產品組合，後續成長關鍵可觀察其新產能到位速度。

華邦電Si-Cap今年開始進入量產，技術是基於DRAM的製程技術，且擁有DRAM技術的IDM競爭同業並不多，在該利基型市場容易取得優勢，公司採Stacking（堆疊）製程，與其他業者採Trench（深溝槽）製程的技術路線不同。公司目前量產產品單位面積電容值約3,300nF/mm²，最新樣品已提升至5,400nF/mm²；隨AI晶片功耗提升、先進封裝朝高密度及薄型化發展，Si-Cap可應用於CoWoS、EMIB等先進封裝及AI電源相關應用。

訂單能見度方面，華邦電目前的主要客戶對其下游客戶的合約為期兩年，公司目前取得的Si-Cap供貨合約期限也不低於兩年，但個別客戶及合約內容不便進一步揭露。

Si-Cap不同於DRAM、NAND等標準型記憶體較容易受到供需及價格循環影響，將持續作為公司記憶體本業以外的新產品布局。

news.Title: 記憶體紅利爆發！傳華邦電員工單季獎金百萬、年薪逾5百萬，公司誠意足
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】Threads流傳出一張疑似華邦電員工的貼文，歌頌公司這一季的季獎金高達100萬元，且以工程師粗估今年可以領到512萬元。記憶體廠通常是用當季的獲利回頭看分紅多少，此舉除意味著，華邦電( 2344 )今年賺超大，羨煞旁人外，相較美光開出來的加薪額度，其實華邦電更有誠意。

貼文上歌頌華邦電提到「哇靠，太扯，偉大的華邦電，這一季季獎金100萬啊，一年的年薪14個月加上4季季獎金，且不含加班部分，用底薪很粗略計算8萬元，8乘上14加上400共計512萬元年薪」。文末並提到，現在跳記憶體廠真的是躺著數錢。

從上述數字去計算，該員工平均攤到每月可領42.7萬元，但其中400萬元是把單季獎金直接乘以四，不代表每季都一定有100萬元，也不一定每位員工都領相同金額。但實際上，華邦電光第二季的營業利益就高達300億元，假設當中的一成就有30億元，若以員工人數快4000人計算，上述數字的確存在真實性。

而相較正在醞釀罷工的美光，華邦電公司派誠意較足，更願意將利潤分享自家員工。受惠於AI浪潮，美光獲利大幅成長，但基層員工的績效獎金（IPP）換算下來僅約2.3個月月薪，美光雖祭出每人100萬感謝金及相當於35至68個月總體獎酬，但工會認為這屬於一次性方案，並不買單，正醞釀大規模罷工潮。

A bull stays the course

Is Sandisk a Millionaire-Maker Stock After Its 2026 Run?
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) has created incredible wealth for investors in 2026, with shares of the flash storage specialist rising 621% this year.

So, investors who bought Sandisk to build a million-dollar portfolio are sitting on nice gains now. The good news for investors is that Sandisk still has room to run higher. Let's look at why it makes sense to buy this growth stock even after the stellar gains it has posted in 2026.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The terrific demand for Sandisk's storage solutions is sustainable

Sandisk's NAND flash storage solutions are in great demand in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. Gartner predicts that global NAND flash revenue will surge by a whopping 372% in 2026, driven by healthy AI data center demand and tight supply.

Sandisk is an important player in the NAND flash market. It controlled 11% of this space in the second quarter of 2026, according to Counterpoint Research. Not surprisingly, Sandisk's revenue and earnings grew at a stunning pace in fiscal 2026 (which ended on July 3). The company's top line shot up by 175% year over year to $20.25 billion. Non-GAAP earnings jumped to $70.88 per share from just $2.99 in the prior year.

Importantly, Sandisk is witnessing healthy growth across all its business segments. Its data center segment revenue jumped by 5.4x in the previous fiscal year to $5.15 billion. The edge business, which is Sandisk's largest segment, saw a jump of almost 3x in revenue in fiscal 2026 to $12.16 billion. Sandisk's edge business includes sales of flash memory for smartphones, personal computers (PCs), and gaming consoles, among others.

The company notes that the edge business has room to expand further, thanks to the growth of on-device AI capabilities in areas such as robotics, automotive, and physical AI. And finally, Sandisk's consumer segment, which includes sales of removable flash memory products to customers, is also in fine shape. The segment's revenue increased by 29% in fiscal 2026 to $2.94 billion, an impressive result given the sharp spike in NAND flash prices.

The good news for Sandisk investors is that the NAND flash supply shortage is going to persist in 2027. Gartner estimates that NAND flash prices could increase by 30% next year, following a 293% jump in 2026. The firm expects the favorable price environment to continue until the end of the decade. Even Sandisk noted in its investor day presentation last month that its non-GAAP operating margin will climb to 75% by fiscal 2030.

Story Continues

That points to a nice bottom-line bump considering that Sandisk's non-GAAP operating margin was at 63% in fiscal 2026. So, there is a strong likelihood of Sandisk stock heading even higher over the long run. Moreover, the stock's attractive valuation makes it a no-brainer buy for growth-oriented investors.

It isn't too late to buy Sandisk

Sandisk's astronomical growth is poised to continue in fiscal 2027. Its revenue is expected to jump 142% to $49 billion, while earnings per share could triple, according to consensus estimates. What's more, Sandisk is trading at 25 times trailing earnings and 8 times forward earnings.

So, growth investors looking to build a million-dollar portfolio can still consider buying Sandisk as its healthy growth potential and cheap valuation can send the stock soaring even after the multibagger gains it has clocked in 2026.

news.Title: Prediction: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Will Hit a $3 Trillion Market Cap Before 2027 Is Over
news.Content:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) is a $2.3 trillion company today, but I think it's destined for a $3 trillion market cap by the end of next year. To meet that target would require the stock to rise by about 30% over the next 15 months. Given that the stock market has averaged annual returns of about 10% over the long term, that would be a solid outperformance, so if I'm right, that would make the stock well worth buying now.

How would Taiwan Semiconductor get there? Simple: It just needs to do exactly what it has told investors it will do.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The road to $3 trillion is clear

Few companies are set to benefit more from the AI infrastructure build-out than Taiwan Semiconductor. It's a chip fabrication company that builds the chips that its customers design. Its clients include nearly every company that makes AI computing chips: Nvidia , Broadcom , and AMD headline the list. Furthermore, companies like Apple and Qualcomm utilize Taiwan Semiconductor to fabricate the chips that they design for smartphones and other devices.

Demand for AI chips is still off the charts, and Taiwan Semiconductor management believes that elevated demand will last through at least 2029 to 2030. As a result, it decided to invest another $100 billion in expanding its U.S. production facilities.

Next year, Wall Street analysts expect TSMC's revenue to grow by 35%. As long as Taiwan Semiconductor can convert that revenue growth into relatively proportional earnings growth, as it has in the past, its returns should be highly correlated to its growth rate, as its stock is reasonably valued.

Taiwan Semiconductor now trades at about 27 times forward earnings, a level typical for big tech stocks. So, it should be able to easily convert earnings growth directly into stock price growth.

So while other AI stocks may have greater upside potential, Taiwan Semiconductor is a fairly safe bet to grow at a market-beating pace throughout 2027. It doesn't really matter which computing unit providers are gaining market share in 2027 and beyond. There's a high chance those winners will be contracting for foundry services with TSMC, which makes it a pretty universal AI investment.

news.Title: Wells Fargo Spots Unexpected Winner in TSMC's 2nm Race
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( NYSE:TSM ) could be preparing another major increase in advanced-chip capacity, and Wells Fargo says the biggest near-term beneficiaries may extend well beyond TSMC itself.

The bank said reports that TSMC could expand 2-nanometer production should be viewed as a potential positive for semiconductor capital-equipment companies, which supply the machinery needed to build increasingly complex chips.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with NVDA.

While we await further confirm and more details (e.g., timing, size, node, etc.), we think this should be viewed as a potentially incremental positive opportunity for semi cap companies, Wells Fargo analyst Joe Quatrochi wrote.

The logic is straightforward.

Building additional 2nm capacity requires significant spending on lithography, deposition, etching, inspection and other highly specialized semiconductor-manufacturing equipment.

That means higher TSMC capacity could translate into another layer of demand for the equipment suppliers supporting its fabs.

Quatrochi also pointed to the so-called Silicon Prairie as a logical location for a potential second U.S. campus because Texas already hosts semiconductor operations from companies including Texas Instruments, Samsung, Coherent and Terafab.

TSMC also operates a design service center in Austin.

The customer list behind 2nm demand is another reason the potential expansion matters.

TSMC's major 2nm customers include Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ), Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD ) and Qualcomm ( NASDAQ:QCOM ).

Google ( NASDAQ:GOOG ), Broadcom, Marvell ( NASDAQ:MRVL ), Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) and OpenAI are also among companies expected to use the advanced process.

Investor Takeaway

For investors, the important signal is not simply that TSMC may build more capacity.

It is that demand for leading-edge manufacturing appears broad enough across smartphones, AI accelerators and custom chips to justify additional investment.

That could extend the semiconductor spending cycle further into equipment suppliers.

But Wells Fargo is still waiting for confirmation around the timing, scale and exact technology involved.

Those details will determine how meaningful the opportunity ultimately becomes.

If TSMC materially raises 2nm capacity, investors should watch whether equipment orders and capital-spending forecasts begin moving higher alongside it.

news.Title: Better Semiconductor Equipment Stock: Applied Materials vs. Lam Research
news.Content:
Semiconductor equipment demand has boomed in recent years, driven by the strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) chips, which explains why shares of Lam Research (NASDAQ: LRCX) and Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) have been in fine form this year.

While Lam stock has risen 84% in 2026, Applied Materials is sitting on slightly higher gains of 89%. However, both semiconductor stocks have pulled back over the past three months. Lam has retreated by 27% since reaching a 52-week high on June 30. Applied Materials stock also hit its 52-week high on that date, and it has lost nearly a third of its value since then.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Savvy investors can consider using their slide as a buying opportunity. After all, sales of semiconductor manufacturing equipment are estimated to jump by 23% in 2026 to $166 billion, according to industry association SEMI. Importantly, spending on semiconductor manufacturing equipment is expected to jump to $201 billion in 2027 and $229.5 billion in 2028.

So, the recent slide in shares of Lam Research and Applied Materials may not last for long. However, which one of these equipment suppliers is the better buy right now? Let's find out.

Strong semiconductor demand has accelerated Applied Materials and Lam Research's growth

Both Lam Research and Applied Materials manufacture wafer and fabrication equipment (WFE). Not surprisingly, their growth rate has picked up recently.

Applied Materials' revenue increased 25% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026 (which ended on July 26) to $9.12 billion. The company's non-GAAP earnings per share rose 41% from the year-ago period to a record $3.50. For comparison, Applied Materials' revenue increased by just 8% in the same quarter last year, while non-GAAP EPS increased by 17%.

AI-fueled chip demand played a key role in boosting Applied Materials' growth. For instance, its revenue from sales of equipment used for manufacturing dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) increased by 52% from last year. Additionally, the company expects revenue from advanced packaging equipment to jump by 70% in 2026, as these tools enable chipmakers to integrate multiple specialized chiplets with memory onto a single platform, allowing AI workloads to run smoothly.

Applied Materials management noted on the August earnings call that "most leading edge logic and DRAM fabs are running at full capacity" at its direct customers. As a result, Applied Materials' customers have announced plans to develop over 10 new fabrication plants. The company has also started negotiating customer contracts for 2030, suggesting it could sustain healthy growth over the long run.

Story Continues

The favorable end-market developments explain why Applied Materials anticipates its fiscal Q4 revenue to increase by 51% year over year to $10.25 billion. Its non-GAAP EPS forecast of $4.02 points to an 85% increase over last year. So, Applied Materials' recent drop is clearly an opportunity for investors to buy a top AI stock before it steps on the gas once again.

Similarly, AI-driven semiconductor demand has been a tailwind for Lam Research. Its revenue in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 (which ended on June 28) increased 30% year over year to $6.72 billion. The company's earnings per share increased 37% year over year to $1.82.

The factors driving Lam's robust growth were similar to those of Applied Materials', with both memory and advanced packaging proving to be tailwinds. Moreover, Lam Research now expects stronger growth in WFE spending this year to the low $150 billion range compared to the prior estimate of $140 billion. Even better, Lam expects strong WFE spending to continue in 2027, which isn't surprising considering the points discussed earlier in the article.

So, it is easy to see why Lam expects a significant acceleration in growth this quarter. The company anticipates a 52% year-over-year increase in revenue to $8.1 billion. What's more, it expects a 71% jump in non-GAAP EPS to $2.15.

As such, there isn't much separating Lam Research and Applied Materials in terms of their financial performance and outlook. In fact, there isn't a major difference between the annual EPS growth that both companies are anticipated to deliver over the long run.

YCharts

Can their valuations help decide the better buy?

With almost identical growth rates and similar catalysts, investors may find it difficult to choose from one of these stocks. That's why we will now take a closer look at their sales and earnings multiples.

Again, there isn't much that separates Lam and Applied Materials even on the valuation front. news.Title: Bottlenecking the Future: TSMC Prices Out the Competition
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd.? Here are five stocks we like better.

TSMC raised its 2-nanometer production target by about 20% to roughly 120,000 wafers monthly, driven by locked-in client commitments rather than speculation.

Advanced 2-nanometer wafers could command about $30,000, a 50% premium over 3-nanometer chips, giving TSMC significant pricing power and margin expansion potential.

Bullish options positioning, minimal short interest, insider stock purchases, and new institutional investments all signal strong confidence in TSMC's growth trajectory.

The market often debates the durability of the semiconductor hardware cycle. Market skeptics point to macroeconomic slowing, cyclical financing, and inventory gluts as reasons to discount chipmakers.

Yet, the leading indicator for global computing infrastructure is telling a different story entirely. If we examine the capital and capacity flows at the foundational layer of chip fabrication, a clearer picture of a sustained, multi-year demand signal is emerging.

→ CarMax Just Gave Investors a Better Reason to Believe in the Turnaround

Expanding the Silicon Highway

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (NYSE: TSM) is actively accelerating its 2-nanometer production timeline, effectively cornering the global advanced computing supply chain.

Instead of pulling back on capital expenditures amid economic uncertainty, the leading chip fabricator is pressing the accelerator, backed by direct commitments from the world's largest technology firms. This divergence between market anxiety and hard production data offers a compelling opportunity for investors evaluating the semiconductor space.

→ Apple, Meta, and SpaceX Are Driving a Device Boom—These 3 Stocks Could Benefit

When a foundry of this scale pulls forward capacity, it does so based on signed agreements, not speculative forecasts. TSMC's shift to accelerate its 2-nanometer production signals that the top tier of the semiconductor market operates independently of standard consumer electronics cycles.

The $30,000 Wafer Toll

To understand the foundational strength of the current semiconductor cycle, we look directly at TSMC's plans for its 2-nanometer node. Recently, production targets for this process were revised upward by roughly 20%, aiming for around 120,000 wafers per month by the end of 2026.

→ 2 Short-Squeeze Candidates Waiting for the Right Catalyst

This target shift from an earlier baseline of 100,000 wafers highlights a critical business reality for the fabrication industry. Semiconductor capital expenditure at this level is demand-driven. Foundries expand capacity because guaranteed, locked-in client orders demand that physical space.

Story Continues

The fundamental advantage here centers on pricing power. Early estimates suggest that an advanced 2-nanometer wafer will command a premium price approaching $30,000. Compared with the 3-nanometer node, which prices around $20,000, this represents a 50% premium. For investors, this pricing dynamic is central to the semiconductor investment thesis.

Moving clients to the latest node lets TSMC organically expand margins even if total global wafer volume growth stabilizes. Foundries operating at the bleeding edge do not compete on price; they compete on physics. By accelerating its 2nm timeline, TSMC widens its lead over competitors, making it the default choice for companies designing next-generation chips.

Captive Clients Pay the Express Toll

A fabrication business's true strength depends entirely on the quality and necessity of its clients. Currently, early tape-outs for the 2-nanometer node are registering at roughly four times the volume seen during the equivalent developmental stage of the previous iteration. For context, a tape-out is the final stage of the chip design process before physical manufacturing begins. This metric is a leading indicator of future revenue visibility.

Captive clients like Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA), and Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) are locked in an architectural arms race. Because training advanced models and operating high-performance computing centers require maximizing silicon efficiency, these developers cannot afford to wait for alternative foundries to catch up. They are often willing to pay a premium to secure early capacity.

This dynamic positions TSMC as a toll road for next-generation hardware. When a single company controls most of the world's supply of its most critical technological component, concerns about a cyclical hardware slowdown lose their weight. The broader semiconductor market might experience inventory cycles in the automotive sector or standard consumer electronics, but the top-tier computing fabrication market operates on an isolated demand curve.

Options Markets Signal Bullish Conviction

Institutional positioning further confirms the thesis. A review of recent options chain data shows implied volatility lingering in the low 30% range, paired with a volume put-call ratio near 0.80. This lack of heavy downside hedging indicates that institutional capital remains firmly anchored to the bullish narrative. Short interest in TSMC stock is virtually nonexistent, representing less than 1% of the total float.

Corporate leadership is signaling a similar confidence. Recent regulatory filings indicate executive open-market purchases, including direct stock acquisitions by the CEO. When an insider allocates personal capital to a stock that is already significantly up, it typically signals internal conviction about forward-looking capacity and revenue pipelines.

Institutional investors seem to share this sentiment, with entities like Silicon Valley Capital Partners recently initiating multi-million-dollar positions to capture the upcoming margin expansion.

From a valuation standpoint, TSMC's forward price-to-earnings ratio in the upper 20s presents an interesting relative discount. While fabless client partners like Advanced Micro Devices trade at forward multiples near 80x, the company building the physical architecture trades at a far more conservative valuation, despite net margins routinely hovering around 50%.

Expansion Friction vs. Leverage

No company operates without friction, and one variable for investors to monitor is the cost of TSMC's geographic diversification. Supply chain reports indicate active evaluations for expanding mega-campus footprints, including potential secondary sites in the United States. Building fabrication facilities outside Taiwan's established ecosystem raises operating costs, exacerbates specialized labor shortages, and complicates logistics. These factors will likely put pressure on gross margins during the initial build-out phase.

However, investors who evaluate TSMC on short-term margin compression alone are overlooking the broader strategic pivot. Spreading production across regions reduces the company's dependence on a single geography, addressing one of the main reasons cautious institutional investors have long discounted the stock.

The unparalleled pricing leverage of the 2-nanometer node will help offset the capital expenditure burden of international expansion. TSMC's recent revenue acceleration, highlighted by a year-over-year jump exceeding 50% in late summer 2026, demonstrates how easily premium pricing can absorb higher operating costs.

Management's upward revision to full-year revenue growth guidance cements this reality. By securing dominant pricing power and locking in multi-year capacity commitments from the world's best-funded technology developers, TSMC has laid the foundation for lasting leadership. For investors watching the hardware cycle, the toll road for the digital economy is getting wider, and the barriers to entry have never been higher.

news.Title: LITE vs. NVTS: Which AI Data Center Stock Is the Better Buy?
news.Content:
Lumentum Holdings LITE and Navitas Semiconductor NVTS are two key players in the AI data center market. They benefit from the growing demand for data centers, artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, and energy-efficient technologies.

Lumentum designs and sells optical and photonic components, such as lasers and optical networking products, which help move data quickly through fiber-optic networks used by cloud and AI data centers. Navitas Semiconductor focuses on Gallium nitride (GaN) and Silicon carbide (SiC) chips used in next-generation AI data centers and energy systems. Its products are used in fast chargers, electric vehicles, and data centers.

LITE or NVTS — Which of these AI Data Center stocks has the greater upside potential? Let's find out.

The Case for LITE Stock

Lumentum is benefiting from strong demand for its optical components and systems, driven by the industry shift to AI workloads and increased data center connectivity. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the company reported a 109% year-over-year revenue surge to $1.01 billion, marking its eighth consecutive quarter of top-line growth. Accelerating adoption of optical links in data centers, driven by AI workloads that demand higher speed and bandwidth, is fueling this momentum.

Key growth drivers include record shipments of 800G cloud transceivers, the launch of next-generation 1.6T modules and strong demand for both EML and CW laser chips. LITE's pump laser shipments surged more than 80% year over year in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, and the company remains effectively sold out despite rapid capacity expansion. Strategic long-term agreements with major customers further secure future demand and support ongoing capital investments.

The market's shift toward near-packaged optics (NPO) and co-packaged optics (CPO) is also playing directly to LITE's strengths. Customers are increasingly adopting these architectures as intermediate steps to full CPO deployment, significantly expanding the total addressable market for optical solutions.

The company is already seeing strong NPO momentum across multiple high-velocity engagements, leveraging its industry-leading laser chip technology. Lumentum expects a fourfold increase in pump laser shipments over the next several quarters and is expanding capacity at its wafer fabs to capture the coming 200-gig and 300-gig lane speed opportunities.

The Case for NVTS Stock

Navitas Semiconductor is becoming a focused high-power semiconductor supplier for AI data centers, grid infrastructure, performance computing and industrial electrification. Its combined GaN and high-voltage SiC portfolio broadens content opportunities across evolving power architectures, while record book-to-bill, multiple customer programs and a richer product mix support growth and margin expansion.

Management highlighted a sequential revenue increase of 22% in the second quarter of 2026, with high-power markets growing more than 50% year over year. Navitas Semiconductor's AI-focused product offerings have established it as a differentiated provider for hyperscalers and telecenter OEMs, with multiple major design wins and ramping programs that will accelerate growth through 2027 and beyond.

The company is securing opportunities across AC-DC power supplies, DC-DC power supplies, battery backup units and compute trays. Several programs are expected to ramp up during the second half of 2026 and continue through 2027. Management said that the initial SiC adoption cycle is already occurring independently of native 800V deployment because higher rack power requires greater efficiency and density.

Sidecar-related programs are expected to begin ramping up in the first half of 2027 and accelerate around midyear. Native 800V systems should create another GaN content increase from mid-to-late 2027 into 2028. Record book-to-bill and backlog extending beyond 2026 support management's expectation for double-digit sequential growth through the second half of 2026.

Story Continues

Price Performance and Valuation of LITE and NVTS

In the year-to-date period, LITE shares have skyrocketed 150%, outperforming Navitas Semiconductor shares, which have risen 64.3%. Lumentum is benefiting from the rapid expansion of AI and cloud infrastructure, which is increasing bandwidth requirements within data centers and accelerating the shift from electrical to optical connectivity.

Despite Navitas Semiconductor expanding its portfolio, revenues remain small relative to operating costs, profitability is still distant and planned spending is rising. Future growth depends on customers completing lengthy qualifications and scaling new AI programs. Competition, foundry dependence and pending litigation add execution risk.

In terms of forward 12-month Price/Sales, LITE shares are trading at 11.66X, lower than NVTS's 48.08X.

Conclusion

NVTS, meanwhile, faces ongoing losses and execution risks as it works to scale its AI-focused power semiconductor programs.

news.Title: NVIDIA Just Turned AI Safety Into a Spending Story and These 3 Stocks Benefit
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Marvell Technology, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform and industry self-regulation could increase AI infrastructure spending by requiring more testing, monitoring and inference computing power.

Analyst Luke Lango highlights Marvell Technology, Arm Holdings and Lumentum Holdings as beneficiaries of a shift from GPU-heavy training toward inference, connectivity and bandwidth demand.

All three stocks depend on continuous model testing and serving rather than frontier AI progress, though rising bond yields and tight liquidity could still pressure their valuations.

NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) spent most of September arguing that AI safety is an engineering problem, not a legal one. On Sept. 28, the company shipped the product to prove it. NVIDIA introduced the Open Agent Safety Platform alongside more than 100 industry partners, pairing open-source access controls with an independent monitoring layer that runs on separate silicon so it can watch an AI agent without living inside it. Jensen Huang framed the launch plainly: AI's potential only gets realized if safety gets solved alongside capability.

Investors hear "safety" and price in a slowdown. Luke Lango of InvestorPlace thinks that reading is backward and that a self-regulation path widens the AI infrastructure spending pipeline rather than narrowing it. That's the setup behind three names he's watching.

→ CarMax Just Gave Investors a Better Reason to Believe in the Turnaround

Self-Regulation Costs More Compute, Not Less

Lango's argument starts with mechanics. If labs agree to evaluate each other's models rather than wait for Washington, every new release triggers another round of testing, monitoring and peer review. All of that runs on hardware.

It also changes the kind of hardware in demand. Slowing the frontier means slowing pre-training, the GPU-heavy part of the stack. Testing and serving models at scale is inference, and it depends less on raw chip power than on moving data efficiently and coordinating many tasks at once. Lango expects that shift from training to inference to define the next six to 12 months of demand, favoring CPUs and connectivity over raw accelerators.

→ Apple, Meta, and SpaceX Are Driving a Device Boom—These 3 Stocks Could Benefit

That's the tension worth watching. Under a safety regime, the AI trade doesn't die. It rotates.

Marvell Technology Sits Where the Bottleneck Moved

Huang made this case himself. At Computex in early June, he called Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) the next trillion-dollar company, pointing to the connectivity that lets thousands of chips behave like one machine.

Story Continues

→ 2 Short-Squeeze Candidates Waiting for the Right Catalyst

Shares jumped more than 32% the next session, the stock's best day on record.

The business has kept pace with the rhetoric. Marvell guided fiscal 2027 revenue to roughly $12 billion and fiscal 2028 to about $18 billion, and the stock has returned over 200% so far in 2026.

It's also well off its highs, trading around 20% below its 52-week peak after an August sell-off. Lango treats that gap as the opportunity, arguing the data center networking names that ran hard, pulled back and held their long-term trend lines are where the shopping list starts.

Arm Holdings Is Selling CPUs Into a CPU Shortage

The second name is Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM), and the pitch is timing.

In March, Arm shipped the AGI CPU, the first production chip in its 35-year history as a licensing business. It runs up to 136 Neoverse V3 cores, is manufactured by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM) on a 3-nanometer node, and Arm claims more than double the performance per rack versus x86 platforms.

Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) co-developed the chip and took first delivery, with OpenAI, Cerebras (NASDAQ: CBRS) and Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) among launch partners.

The CPU went from afterthought to orchestration layer as agentic workloads spread. That resurgence has already carried Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) up roughly 280% over the past year and put a fresh bid under Intel (NASDAQ: INTC). Lango sees Arm as the higher-torque version of the same trade, because it's converting from royalties into silicon revenue right as AI inference demand accelerates.

Lumentum Holds the Bandwidth Bottleneck

Copper can only carry so much. As GPUs multiply and constantly talk to one another, data centers are swapping copper interconnects for optics, photonics and fiber. That's the core business of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE).

The numbers reflect it. Lumentum closed fiscal 2026 with $1.01 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and guided the current quarter to a midpoint near $1.25 billion.

NVIDIA committed $2 billion to expand Lumentum's capacity and deepen joint development on data center optics.

Unlike Marvell and Arm, this stock hasn't corrected so much as stalled.

Lango reads the sideways action as consolidation ahead of a move rather than a broken growth story, and the AI safety stocks framing gives it a second tailwind: more model-checking means more traffic between chips, and more traffic means wider optical highways.

Self-Regulation Keeps the Capital Spending Cycle Intact

Marvell, Arm and Lumentum are three pieces of one machine: custom silicon, orchestration and bandwidth. None of them depends on the frontier labs racing faster. They depend on models being served, tested and checked constantly, which is precisely what self-regulation would institutionalize.

What the setup does depend on is CapEx discipline holding and the macro backdrop easing enough for high-multiple hardware names to re-rate. If the 10-year yield stays elevated and liquidity stays tight, good numbers may keep getting offset by a shrinking multiple, exactly as they have been.

Stay focused on where the marginal compute dollar goes, because that is what moves these stocks far more than the next doomsday headline.

For more on the physical AI wave and the infrastructure Elon Musk is assembling around it, see Luke Lango's special reports on Elon Musk, SpaceX and the next stage of AI.

news.Title: KLAC's Backlog Surges on AI Demand: Can It Outpace AMAT & ASML?
news.Content:
KLA Corporation KLAC is benefiting from a strong backlog and improving semiconductor equipment demand, supported by accelerating Artificial Intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments and rising spending across leading-edge chip manufacturing. KLAC's backlog increased to $12.57 billion at the end of fiscal 2026 from $7.86 billion a year earlier, primarily driven by demand tied to the AI infrastructure buildout. The strong order pipeline improves revenue visibility and positions KLAC to capitalize on continued investments in foundry/logic, memory and advanced packaging, while strengthening its competitive position against Applied Materials AMAT and ASML Holding ASML.

The broader semiconductor equipment environment is also strengthening. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, KLAC raised its calendar 2026 wafer fabrication equipment market expectation, including advanced packaging, to the low-$150-billion range, up from its earlier view of more than $140 billion and compared with roughly $120 billion in calendar 2025. Management expects broad-based investments across leading-edge logic, foundry, DRAM, high-bandwidth memory (HBM), NAND and advanced packaging to support continued capacity expansion. KLAC expects second-half calendar 2026 revenues to increase roughly 20% from the first half as additional supply becomes available, supporting continued sequential growth into calendar 2027.

Rising semiconductor complexity is increasing demand for KLAC's inspection, metrology and yield-management solutions. Management expects its semiconductor process-control business to grow at least a few percentage points faster than the overall company as high-performance computing becomes a larger portion of semiconductor spending. KLAC also expects several new greenfield fabs in 2027, creating demand not only for technology upgrades but also for incremental equipment installations. Broadening logic investment, continued HBM adoption, advanced packaging and new fab construction should therefore expand KLAC's addressable opportunity.

Advanced packaging provides another important catalyst. KLAC expects advanced-packaging process-control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, up more than 70% year over year, almost twice the growth rate of the advanced-packaging market. Its competitive position is also supported by complex process control, algorithmic expertise and a global network of roughly 1,600-1,700 applications engineers.

KLAC Faces Tough Competition

Story Continues

Applied Materials is benefiting from the same AI-driven semiconductor equipment upcycle. AMAT expects leading-edge foundry/logic, DRAM and advanced packaging to account for roughly 80% of wafer fab equipment growth in 2026 and 2027. Its process diagnostics and control business is expected to grow more than 50% in 2026, supported by e-beam and optical inspection demand. Applied Materials is also expanding manufacturing capacity, targeting the ability to double quarterly system output from current levels by 2028, while some customer discussions now extend to 2030.

ASML Holding is likewise benefiting from accelerating capacity additions across logic and memory. In its second-quarter 2026 update, the company expects full-year 2026 advanced foundry/logic revenues to rise about 25%, memory revenues to increase 75% and EUV revenues to grow roughly 45%. ASML also expects DUV, metrology and inspection revenues to increase about 25% in 2026, supported by higher process-control intensity and greater adoption of optical metrology and e-beam inspection. ASML said it was close to receiving the orders required for 2027 and plans to add roughly 30% to its Low-NA EUV capacity in 2027, while investigating another potential 30% capacity increase in 2028. These capacity investments could intensify competitive pressure on KLAC as semiconductor spending and process-control requirements continue to rise.
